bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑第246卷

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 246
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 246

sentences.zh: 【唐紀六十二】起著雍敦牂，盡玄默閹茂，凡五年。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 62] From the Gengshen year, twelfth month, through the Gengzi year, twelfth month—in all, five years.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records 62] This section runs from the twelfth month of the Gengshen year through the twelfth month of the Gengzi year, a span of five years.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，甲子，李石入朝，中塗有盜射之，微傷。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, day jiazi: Li Shi entered court; on the way bandits shot at him, and he was slightly wounded.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first day of the first month, Li Shi was on his way to court when assassins fired on him and wounded him slightly.

sentences.zh: 左右奔散，石馬驚，馳歸第。

translations.literal: His attendants scattered; Shi's horse panicked, and he galloped back to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants fled in every direction; his horse bolted, and he raced home to his mansion.

sentences.zh: 又有盜邀擊於坊門，斷其馬尾，僅而得免。

translations.literal: Again bandits waylaid him at the ward gate, severed his horse's tail, and he barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: At the ward gate more assailants ambushed him and hacked off his horse's tail; he escaped only by a hair's breadth.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，大驚，命神策六軍遣兵防衞，敕中外捕盜甚急，竟無所獲。

translations.literal: The emperor heard of it and was greatly alarmed; he ordered the six Shence armies to send troops for protection and commanded urgent pursuit of the bandits throughout the realm, yet none were captured.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned of the attack he was deeply shaken. He ordered the six Shence armies to post guards and launched a sweeping manhunt, but no culprits were ever found.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，百官入朝者九人而已。

translations.literal: On day yichou, only nine officials came to court.
translations.idiomatic: On the following day only nine officials dared attend court.

sentences.zh: 京城數日方安。

translations.literal: Only after several days did the capital grow calm.
translations.idiomatic: Several days passed before the capital regained its composure.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，追贈故齊王湊爲懷懿太子。

translations.literal: On day dingmao, the late Prince of Qi, Cou, was posthumously enfeoffed as the Huaiyi Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao day the deceased Prince of Qi, Cou, was posthumously honored as Crown Prince Huaiyi.

sentences.zh: 戊申，以鹽鐵轉運使、戸部尚書楊嗣復，戸部侍郎、判戸部李玨並同平章事，判、使如故。

translations.literal: On day wushen, Yang Sifu, Commissioner of the Salt and Iron Transport and Minister of Revenue, and Li Jue, Vice Minister of Revenue and acting head of the ministry, were both made Grand Councilors of the Same Rank; their acting posts and commissionerships remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen day Yang Sifu, salt-and-iron transport commissioner and minister of revenue, and Li Jue, vice minister of revenue with charge of the ministry, were both appointed co–grand councilors while retaining their existing portfolios.

sentences.zh: 嗣復，於陵之子也。

translations.literal: Sifu was a son of Yu Ling.
translations.idiomatic: Sifu was the son of the former chief minister Yu Ling.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎、同平章事李石，承甘露之亂，人情危懼，宦官恣橫，忘身徇國，故紀綱粗立。

translations.literal: Li Shi, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor of the Same Rank, after the Sweet Dew turmoil, when the people were fearful and eunuchs ran rampant, forgot himself in service to the state, and thus the basic order was roughly restored.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi, vice director of the Secretariat and co–grand councilor, had after the Sweet Dew coup held the state together while the court lived in terror and eunuchs ruled unchecked; by risking his own life for the realm he had at least shored up the foundations of government.

sentences.zh: 仇士良深惡之，潛遣盜殺之，不果。

translations.literal: Qiu Shiliang deeply hated him and secretly sent assassins to kill him, but they did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Shiliang loathed him and secretly hired killers, yet the plot failed.

sentences.zh: 石懼，累表稱疾辭位。

translations.literal: Shi was afraid and repeatedly memorialized, pleading illness to resign his post.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing for his life, Shi repeatedly asked to step down on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 上深知其故而無如之何。

translations.literal: The emperor knew full well the reason yet could do nothing about it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor understood perfectly why Shi wanted out but was powerless to help him.

sentences.zh: 丙子，以石同平章事，充荊南節度使。

translations.literal: On day bingzi, Shi was made Grand Councilor of the Same Rank and appointed military governor of Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi day Shi was named co–grand councilor and sent out as military governor of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 陳夷行性介直，惡楊嗣復爲人，毎議政事，多相抵斥。

translations.literal: Chen Yixing's nature was stern and upright; he detested Yang Sifu's character, and whenever they discussed state affairs they mostly clashed.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yixing was stiff and upright by nature and despised Yang Sifu; in council they quarreled at almost every turn.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，夷行以足疾辭位，不許。

translations.literal: On day renchen, Yixing resigned on account of foot ailment; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen day Yixing tried to resign because of a foot ailment, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 上命起居舍人魏謨獻其祖文貞公笏，鄭覃曰：「在人不在笏。」

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Wei Mo, Master of the Diaries, to present the ivory tablet of his grandfather, the Duke of Wenzhen; Zheng Tan said: "What matters is the man, not the tablet."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Wei Mo of the Imperial Diary to present the court tablet of his grandfather, Duke Wenzhen. Zheng Tan remarked, "What we honor is the man, not the tablet."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「亦甘棠之比也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "It is also like the sweet pear tree."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "Even so, it is like the sweet-pear tree under which the people still remember a worthy ruler."

sentences.zh: 楊嗣復欲援進李宗閔，恐爲鄭覃所沮，乃先令宦官諷上。

translations.literal: Yang Sifu wished to advance Li Zongmin and, fearing obstruction from Zheng Tan, first had eunuchs hint to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sifu wanted to bring Li Zongmin back into office but feared Zheng Tan would block it, so he had eunuchs sound out the emperor first.

sentences.zh: 上臨朝，謂宰相曰：「宗閔積年在外，宜與一官。」

translations.literal: At court the emperor said to the chief ministers: "Zongmin has been abroad many years; he should be given an office."
translations.idiomatic: At audience the emperor told his chief ministers, "Zongmin has been in exile for years; it is time to give him a post."

sentences.zh: 鄭覃曰：「陛下若憐宗閔之遠，止可移近北數百里，不宜再用。

translations.literal: Zheng Tan said: "If Your Majesty pities Zongmin's distance, he may be moved a few hundred li nearer to the north, but he should not be employed again.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tan objected: "If Your Majesty pities his exile, move him a few hundred li closer to the capital—but do not put him back in power.

sentences.zh: 用之，臣請先避位。」

translations.literal: If he is used, this subject asks first to yield his seat."
translations.idiomatic: If you appoint him, I beg leave to resign first."

sentences.zh: 陳夷行曰：「宗閔向以朋黨亂政，陛下何愛此纖人！」

translations.literal: Chen Yixing said: "Zongmin formerly threw the government into disorder through faction; why does Your Majesty favor this petty man!"
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yixing said, "Zongmin once wrecked the government with his faction. Why spare such a contemptible figure?"

sentences.zh: 楊嗣復曰：「事貴得中，不可但徇愛憎。」

translations.literal: Yang Sifu said: "Affairs value hitting the mean; one cannot simply indulge love and hate."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sifu countered, "Policy should strike the middle course; Your Majesty must not rule by personal likes and dislikes alone."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「可與一州。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "He may be given a prefecture."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Very well—give him a prefecture."

sentences.zh: 覃曰：「與州太優，止可洪州司馬耳。」

translations.literal: Tan said: "A prefecture is too generous; he should receive only the post of Hengzhou vice prefect."
translations.idiomatic: Tan insisted, "A prefecture is too grand; make him only vice prefect of Hongzhou."

sentences.zh: 因與嗣復互相抵訐以爲黨。

translations.literal: Thereupon he and Sifu reviled each other as if forming factions.
translations.idiomatic: Tan and Sifu then traded insults like rival party chiefs.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「與一州無傷。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Giving a prefecture does no harm."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "A prefecture will do no harm."

sentences.zh: 覃等退，上謂起居郎周敬復、舍人魏謨曰：「宰相喧爭如此，可乎？」

translations.literal: When Tan and the others withdrew, the emperor said to Zhou Jingfu, Gentleman of the Imperial Diary, and Wei Mo, Secretariat Drafter: "Chief ministers shouting at each other like this—can it be right?"
translations.idiomatic: After Tan and his allies left, the emperor asked Zhou Jingfu of the diary staff and Wei Mo of the secretariat, "Is it fitting for chief ministers to brawl in open court like this?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「誠爲不可。

translations.literal: They replied: "It truly cannot be allowed.
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "Indeed it is not.

sentences.zh: 然覃等盡忠憤激，不自覺耳。」

translations.literal: Yet Tan and the others were wholly loyal and inflamed with zeal, unaware of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Still, Tan and the others were acting from loyal indignation and hardly knew how far they had gone."

sentences.zh: 丁酉，以衡州司馬李宗閔爲杭州刺史。

translations.literal: On day dingyou, Li Zongmin, Vice Prefect of Hengzhou, was made Prefect of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou day Li Zongmin was promoted from vice prefect of Hengzhou to prefect of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 李固言與楊嗣復、李玨善，故引居大政以排鄭覃、陳夷行，毎議政之際，是非鋒起，上不能決也。

translations.literal: Li Guyin was on good terms with Yang Sifu and Li Jue; therefore he brought them into high office to exclude Zheng Tan and Chen Yixing. Whenever policy was debated, rights and wrongs flared like blades, and the emperor could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guyin was allied with Yang Sifu and Li Jue and had installed them in power to shut out Zheng Tan and Chen Yixing. Council sessions dissolved into shouting matches over every issue, and the emperor could settle nothing.

sentences.zh: 三月，牂柯寇涪州清溪鎮，鎮兵擊卻之。

translations.literal: Third month: Zangke raided Qingxi Town in Fuzhou; the garrison troops beat them back.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the Zangke people attacked Qingxi in Fuzhou; local troops drove them off.

sentences.zh: 初，太和之末，杜悰爲鳳翔節度使，有詔沙汰僧尼。

translations.literal: Earlier, at the end of the Taihe era, Du Cong was military governor of Fengxiang; there was an edict to purge monks and nuns.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Taihe reign Du Cong governed Fengxiang when the court ordered a purge of monks and nuns.

sentences.zh: 時有五色雲見於岐山，近法門寺，民間訛言佛骨降祥，以僧尼不安之故。

translations.literal: At the time five-colored clouds appeared on Mount Qi near Famen Monastery; among the people a false rumor spread that Buddha's relics had sent an auspicious sign because the monks and nuns were unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Five-colored clouds then appeared over Mount Qi near Famen Monastery, and rumor had it that the Buddha's relics were signaling approval because the clergy were being harassed.

sentences.zh: 監軍欲奏之，悰曰：「雲物變色，何常之有！

translations.literal: The army supervisor wished to memorialize it; Cong said: "Clouds change color—what is so unusual about that!
translations.idiomatic: The army supervisor wanted to report the omen, but Cong said, "Clouds change color all the time—what is remarkable about that?

sentences.zh: 佛若果愛僧尼，當見於京師。」

translations.literal: If the Buddha truly loved monks and nuns, the sign should appear in the capital."
translations.idiomatic: If the Buddha truly cared for the clergy, let the sign appear in the capital."

sentences.zh: 未幾，獲白兔，監軍又欲奏之，曰：「此西方之瑞也。」

translations.literal: Before long a white hare was caught; the supervisor again wished to memorialize it, saying: "This is an auspice of the West."
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward a white hare was caught. The supervisor again wanted to report it as "an omen from the western quarter."

sentences.zh: 悰曰：「野獸未馴，且宜畜之。」

translations.literal: Cong said: "The wild beast is not yet tame; for the time being it should be kept alive."
translations.idiomatic: Cong replied, "The creature is still wild—keep it alive for now."

sentences.zh: 旬日而斃。

translations.literal: Within ten days it died.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days it was dead.

sentences.zh: 監軍不悅，以爲掩蔽聖德，獨畫圖獻之。

translations.literal: The supervisor was displeased, thinking that Cong had concealed the sage's virtue; he alone painted a picture and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: The supervisor was angry, accusing Cong of hiding heaven's favor, and sent up only his own painted record of the hare.

sentences.zh: 及鄭注代心宗鎮鳳翔，奏紫雲見，又獻白雉。

translations.literal: When Zheng Zhu replaced Xin Zong as governor of Fengxiang, he reported purple clouds and also presented a white pheasant.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Zhu took over Fengxiang from Xin Zong he reported purple clouds and sent up a white pheasant as well.

sentences.zh: 是歳，八月，有甘露降於紫宸殿前櫻桃之上，上親采而嘗之，百官稱賀。

translations.literal: That year, in the eighth month, sweet dew fell on the cherry trees before the Zichen Hall; the emperor personally gathered and tasted it, and the hundred officials offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: That same year, in the eighth month, sweet dew appeared on the cherries before the Hall of Purple Reach. The emperor picked and tasted it himself while the whole court congratulated him.

sentences.zh: 其十一月，遂有金吾甘露之變。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month came the Sweet Dew incident at the Golden Guards.
translations.idiomatic: By the eleventh month the Sweet Dew coup at the Golden Guards had erupted.

sentences.zh: 及悰爲工部尚書、判度支，河中奏騶虞見，百官稱賀。

translations.literal: When Cong became Minister of Works with charge of the treasury, Hezhong reported the sighting of a zouyu, and the hundred officials congratulated.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Cong was minister of works with charge of the treasury, Hezhong reported a zouyu, and officials again offered congratulations.

sentences.zh: 上謂悰曰：「李訓、鄭注皆因瑞以售其亂，乃知瑞物非國之慶。

translations.literal: The emperor said to Cong: "Li Xun and Zheng Zhu both used auspices to market their rebellion; thus one knows that lucky objects are not the state's blessing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Cong, "Li Xun and Zheng Zhu both used omens to peddle treason. That shows lucky signs are no blessing to the state.

sentences.zh: 卿前在鳳翔，不奏白兔，真先覺也。」

translations.literal: When you were earlier in Fengxiang and did not memorialize the white hare, you truly foresaw."
translations.idiomatic: When you refused to report the white hare in Fengxiang, you saw the danger before anyone else."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「昔河出圖，伏羲以畫八卦；

translations.literal: He replied: "Of old the Yellow River produced a chart and Fuxi drew the Eight Trigrams from it;
translations.idiomatic: Cong answered, "In antiquity the Yellow River sent forth a chart and Fuxi drew the Eight Trigrams from it;

sentences.zh: 洛出書，大禹以敘九疇，皆有益於人，故足尚也。

translations.literal: the Luo produced a writing and Yu the Great arranged the Nine Categories—all benefited mankind, and therefore they are truly worthy of honor.
translations.idiomatic: the Luo sent forth a text and Yu the Great arranged the Nine Categories—each truly served mankind, and that is why they deserve reverence.

sentences.zh: 至於禽獸草木之瑞，何時無之！

translations.literal: As for auspices among birds, beasts, plants, and trees—when have they ever been lacking!
translations.idiomatic: As for lucky birds, beasts, plants, and trees—when are they ever absent?

sentences.zh: 劉聰桀逆，黃龍三見；

translations.literal: Liu Cong was cruel and rebellious, yet yellow dragons appeared thrice;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong was vicious and rebellious, yet yellow dragons appeared three times;

sentences.zh: 石季龍暴虐，得蒼麟十六、白鹿七，以駕芝蓋。

translations.literal: Shi Jilong was violent and tyrannical, yet obtained sixteen azure qilin and seven white deer to draw his spirit canopy.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jilong was brutal and cruel, yet gathered sixteen azure qilin and seven white deer to pull his sacred carriage.

sentences.zh: 以是觀之，瑞豈在德！

translations.literal: Viewed in this light, do auspices depend on virtue!
translations.idiomatic: From this one sees that omens have nothing to do with virtue!

sentences.zh: 玄宗嘗爲潞州別駕，及即位，潞州奏十九瑞，玄宗曰：『朕在潞州，惟知勤職業，此等瑞物，皆不知也。』

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong once served as vice prefect of Luzhou; when he took the throne, Luzhou reported nineteen auspices. Xuanzong said: "When I was in Luzhou I knew only diligence in duty; I knew nothing of such lucky things."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong had once been vice prefect of Luzhou. After his accession Luzhou reported nineteen omens. Xuanzong said, "While I was in Luzhou I knew only hard work in office—I never heard of any of these lucky signs."

sentences.zh: 願陛下專門以百姓富安爲國慶，自餘不足取也。」

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty would devote yourself solely to the people's wealth and peace as the state's celebration; the rest is not worth taking."
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty to take the people's prosperity and security alone as the true blessing of the realm and to disregard everything else."

sentences.zh: 上善之，他日，謂宰相曰：「時和年豐，是爲上瑞；

translations.literal: The emperor approved. Another day he told the chief ministers: "Seasons in harmony and years abundant—those are the supreme auspices;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased. On another day he told his chief ministers, "Mild seasons and rich harvests are the highest omens;

sentences.zh: 嘉禾靈芝，誠何益於事！」

translations.literal: fine grain and numinous fungus—what real good do they do!"
translations.idiomatic: fine grain and spirit fungus—what do they actually accomplish?"

sentences.zh: 宰相因言：「《春秋》紀災異以儆人君，而不書祥瑞，用此故也！」

translations.literal: The chief ministers then said: "The Spring and Autumn Annals records disasters and anomalies to warn rulers but does not record lucky signs—for this very reason!"
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers added, "The Spring and Autumn Annals records disasters and portents to warn rulers but never records lucky signs—for exactly this reason!"

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，乙亥，詔：「諸道有瑞，皆無得以聞，亦勿申牒所司。

translations.literal: Summer, fifth month, day yihai, an edict: "Wherever circuits have auspices, none may be reported, nor may memorials be sent to the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on yihai day in the fifth month, an edict declared: "No circuit may report auspicious omens or send memorials about them to the relevant offices.

sentences.zh: 其臘饗太廟及饗太清宮，元日受朝奏祥瑞，皆停。」

translations.literal: At the winter sacrifice in the Imperial Ancestral Temple and the sacrifice at the Temple of the Grand Ultimate, and at the New Year's audience when auspices were reported—all were suspended."
translations.idiomatic: Reports of omens at the winter sacrifices in the ancestral temple and at the Temple of the Grand Ultimate, and at the New Year's audience, were all abolished."

sentences.zh: 初，靈武節度使王晏平自盜贓七千餘緡，上以其父智興有功，免死，長流康州。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wang Yanping, military governor of Lingwu, had embezzled more than seven thousand strings of cash; because his father Zhixing had rendered merit, the emperor spared his life and exiled him far to Kangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wang Yanping, military governor of Lingwu, had embezzled more than seven thousand strings of cash. Because his father Zhixing had served the dynasty well, the emperor spared his life and banished him to distant Kangzhou.

sentences.zh: 晏平密請於魏、鎮、幽三節度使，使上表雪己。

translations.literal: Yanping secretly asked the military governors of Wei, Zhen, and You to memorialize clearing his name.
translations.idiomatic: Yanping secretly persuaded the governors of Wei, Zhen, and You to petition the throne on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 上不得已，六月，壬寅，改永州司戸。

translations.literal: The emperor had no choice; sixth month, day renyin, he was changed to registrar of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reluctantly agreed; on renyin day in the sixth month Yanping was reassigned as registrar of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 八月，己亥，嘉王運薨。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day jihai: Prince Jia Yun died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on jihai day, Prince Jia Yun died.

sentences.zh: 太子永之母王德妃無寵，爲楊賢妃所譖而死。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Yong's mother, Consort Wang the Virtuous, was without favor and died after slander by the Worthy Consort Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Yong's mother, Virtuous Consort Wang, had fallen from favor and died after Worthy Consort Yang slandered her.

sentences.zh: 太子頗好游宴，暱近小人，賢妃日夜毀之。

translations.literal: The crown prince greatly loved feasting and travel and was intimate with petty men; the Worthy Consort slandered him day and night.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince loved feasts and outings and kept company with low characters, while the Worthy Consort denounced him to the emperor day and night.

sentences.zh: 九月，壬戌，上開延英，召宰相及兩省、御史、郎官，疏太子過惡，議廢之，曰：「是宜爲天子乎？」

translations.literal: Ninth month, day renxu: the emperor opened court at Yanying, summoned chief ministers and officials of the two secretariats, the censorate, and the bureau directors, set forth the crown prince's faults, and discussed deposing him, saying: "Is such a man fit to be Son of Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: On renxu day in the ninth month the emperor convened the Yanying Hall, summoned chief ministers and officials of both secretariats, the censorate, and the directorates, listed the crown prince's offenses, and debated deposing him. "Is this the sort of man who should become emperor?" he asked.

sentences.zh: 群臣皆言：「太子年少，容有改過。

translations.literal: The ministers all said: "The crown prince is young; he may yet reform.
translations.idiomatic: The officials replied, "The crown prince is still young; he may yet mend his ways.

sentences.zh: 國本至重，豈可輕動！」

translations.literal: The foundation of the state is supremely weighty—how can it be lightly moved!"
translations.idiomatic: The heir is the foundation of the realm—he must not be cast aside lightly!"

sentences.zh: 御史中丞狄兼謨論之尤切，至於涕切。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Di Jianmo argued most urgently, even to the point of weeping bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: Vice censor-in-chief Di Jianmo pleaded most fiercely, weeping as he spoke.

sentences.zh: 給事中韋溫曰：「陛下惟一子，不教，陷之至是，豈獨太子之過乎！」

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Wei Wen said: "Your Majesty has only this one son; having failed to instruct him, you have brought him to this—how is it the crown prince's fault alone!"
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Wei Wen said, "Your Majesty has only this one son. Having failed to teach him, you have driven him to this pass—how can the fault be his alone?"

sentences.zh: 癸亥，翰林學士六人、神策六軍軍使十六人復上表論之，上意稍解。

translations.literal: On day guihai, six Hanlin academicians and sixteen army supervisors of the six Shence armies again memorialized on the matter; the emperor's mind eased somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai day six Hanlin scholars and sixteen Shence army commanders submitted further memorials, and the emperor's resolve began to soften.

sentences.zh: 是夕，太子始得歸少陽院。

translations.literal: That evening the crown prince was at last able to return to the Shaoyang Quarter.
translations.idiomatic: That night the crown prince was finally allowed back to the Shaoyang residence.

sentences.zh: 如京使王少華等及宦官、宮人坐流死者數十人。

translations.literal: Wang Shaohua and others of the capital envoys, together with eunuchs and palace women implicated, numbered several tens who were exiled or executed.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen people—including capital envoy Wang Shaohua, eunuchs, and palace women—were exiled or executed in the affair.

sentences.zh: 義武節度使張璠在鎮十五年，爲幽、鎮所憚。

translations.literal: Zhang Fan, military governor of Yiwu, had been in the command fifteen years and was feared by You and Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fan had governed Yiwu for fifteen years, and the northeastern circuits of You and Zhen feared him.

sentences.zh: 及有疾，請入朝，朝廷未及制置，疾甚，戒其子元益舉族歸朝，毋得效河北故事。

translations.literal: When he fell ill he asked to enter court; the court had not yet made arrangements when his illness grew severe; he admonished his son Yuanyi to bring the whole clan back to court and not imitate the Hebei precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill he asked to come to court. Before the capital could act his condition worsened, and he warned his son Yuanyi to bring the whole clan back to the capital and not follow the Hebei custom of passing command within the family.

sentences.zh: 及薨，軍中欲立元益，觀察留後李士季不可，眾殺之，又殺大將十餘人。

translations.literal: When he died the army wished to install Yuanyi; Acting Observation Commissioner Li Shiji refused; the crowd killed him and also killed more than ten great generals.
translations.idiomatic: After his death the troops wanted to install Yuanyi, but acting observation commissioner Li Shiji opposed them and was killed, along with more than ten senior generals.

sentences.zh: 壬申，以易州刺史李仲遷爲義武節度使。

translations.literal: On day renshen, Li Zhongqian, prefect of Yi, was made military governor of Yiwu.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen day Li Zhongqian, prefect of Yi, was appointed military governor of Yiwu.

sentences.zh: 義武馬軍都虞候何清朝自拔歸朝，癸酉，以爲儀州刺史。

translations.literal: He Qingchao, chief adjutant of the Yiwu horse army, came over to the court of his own accord; on day guiyou he was made prefect of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He Qingchao, chief adjutant of the Yiwu cavalry, defected to the court; on guiyou day he was made prefect of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以義昌節度使李彥佐在鎮久，甲戌，以德州刺史劉約爲節度副使，欲以代之。

translations.literal: The court, because Li Yanzuo, military governor of Yichang, had long been in command, on day jiaxu made Liu Yue, prefect of De, deputy military governor, intending to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Li Yanzuo had held Yichang too long, on jiaxu day the court named Dezhou prefect Liu Yue his deputy with the intention of replacing him.

sentences.zh: 開成以來，神策將吏遷官，多不聞奏，直牒中書令覆奏施行，遷改殆元虛日。

translations.literal: Since the Kaicheng era, promotions of Shence officers and clerks were often not reported to the throne; they simply sent documents to the Secretariat for re-memorial and implementation, and transfers were almost daily.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Kaicheng era Shence officers had often been promoted without imperial review, their orders going straight to the Secretariat for confirmation, so that transfers came almost every day.

sentences.zh: 癸未，始詔神策將吏改官皆先奏聞，狀至中書，然後檢勘施行。

translations.literal: On day guiwei, it was first decreed that all Shence promotions must first be reported; when the memorial reached the Secretariat, only then was it examined and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei day an edict required every Shence promotion to be reported to the throne first; only after the memorial reached the Secretariat could it be checked and executed.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，易定監軍奏軍中不納李仲遷，請以張元益爲留後。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month: the army supervisor of Yiding memorialized that the troops would not accept Li Zhongqian and asked that Zhang Yuanyi be made acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, the Yiding army supervisor reported that the troops refused Li Zhongqian and asked that Zhang Yuanyi be made acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 太子永猶不悛，庚子，暴薨，謚曰莊恪。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Yong still did not reform; on day gengzi he died suddenly; his posthumous title was Zhuangke.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Yong still would not mend his ways; on gengzi day he died suddenly and was given the posthumous name Zhuangke.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，以左金吾大將軍郭旼爲邠寧節度使。

translations.literal: On day yisi, Guo Min, great general of the Left Golden Guards, was made military governor of Binning.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi day Guo Min, great general of the Left Golden Guards, was appointed military governor of Binning.

sentences.zh: 宰相議發兵討易定。

translations.literal: The chief ministers discussed sending troops to punish Yiding.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers debated sending troops against Yiding.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「易定地狹人貧，軍資半仰度支。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Yiding's territory is narrow and its people poor; half its military supplies depend on the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Yiding is small and poor; half its supplies come from the central treasury.

sentences.zh: 急之則靡所不爲，緩之則自生變。

translations.literal: If pressed hard they will stop at nothing; if handled gently they will change of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Press them hard and they will do anything; move slowly and they will sort themselves out.

sentences.zh: 但謹備四境以俟之。」

translations.literal: Only carefully guard the four borders and wait."
translations.idiomatic: Simply guard the borders and wait."

sentences.zh: 乃除張元益代州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhang Yuanyi was appointed prefect of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: The court then appointed Zhang Yuanyi prefect of Dai.

sentences.zh: 頃之，軍中果有異議，乃上表以不便李仲遷爲辭，朝廷爲之罷仲遷。

translations.literal: Before long the army indeed had internal dissent and memorialized on the pretext that Li Zhongqian was unsuitable; the court thereupon removed Zhongqian.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the garrison split, citing Li Zhongqian's unsuitability, and the court withdrew his appointment.

sentences.zh: 十一月，壬戌，詔俟元益出定州，其義武將士始謀立元益者，皆赦不問。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day renxu: an edict said that when Yuanyi left Dingzhou, the Yiwu officers and soldiers who had first plotted to install Yuanyi would all be pardoned without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu day in the eleventh month an edict promised that once Yuanyi left Dingzhou, the Yiwu soldiers who had plotted to install him would all be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 以義昌節度使李彥佐爲天平節度使，以劉約爲義昌節度使。

translations.literal: Li Yanzuo, military governor of Yichang, was made military governor of Tianping; Liu Yue was made military governor of Yichang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yanzuo was transferred from Yichang to Tianping, and Liu Yue was made military governor of Yichang.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，張元益出定州。

translations.literal: On day dingmao, Zhang Yuanyi left Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao day Zhang Yuanyi departed Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 庚午，上問翰林學士柳公權以外議，對曰：「郭旼除邠寧，外間頗以爲疑。」

translations.literal: On day gengwu, the emperor asked Hanlin academician Liu Gongquan about outside opinion; he replied: "Guo Min's appointment to Binning has aroused considerable suspicion outside."
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu day the emperor asked Hanlin scholar Liu Gongquan what people were saying outside the palace. Liu answered, "Guo Min's appointment to Binning has stirred widespread unease."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「旼，尚父之侄，太后叔父，在官無過，自金吾作小鎮，外間何尤焉？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Min is a nephew of the Duke of Shangfu and the empress dowager's uncle-by-marriage; in office he has been without fault. From the Golden Guards to a small command—what grievance can there be outside?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Min is Shangfu's nephew and the empress dowager's uncle. He has done nothing wrong in office. Moving him from the Golden Guards to a small circuit—what is there for people to complain about?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「非謂旼不應爲節度使也。

translations.literal: He replied: "It is not that Min ought not to be made military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Liu answered, "I do not mean Min is unfit to be a military governor.

sentences.zh: 聞陛下近取旼二女入宮，有之乎？」

translations.literal: I have heard that Your Majesty recently took two of Min's daughters into the palace—is this so?"
translations.idiomatic: But I hear Your Majesty recently took two of his daughters into the palace. Is that true?"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「然，入參太皇太后耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "It is so; they entered to attend the Grand Empress Dowager."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Yes—they were brought in to serve the grand empress dowager."

sentences.zh: 公權曰：「外間不知，皆雲旼納女後宮，故得方鎮。」

translations.literal: Gongquan said: "Those outside do not know this; all say Min presented daughters to the rear palace and thereby obtained a commandery."
translations.idiomatic: Gongquan said, "People outside do not know that. They all say Min traded his daughters for a military commission."

sentences.zh: 上俯首良久曰：「然則奈何？」

translations.literal: The emperor bowed his head a long while and said: "Then what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor lowered his head for a long time and asked, "Then what can be done?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「獨有自南內遣歸其家，則外議自息矣」是日，太皇太后遣中使送二女還旼家。

translations.literal: He replied: "There is only sending them back from the Southern Inner Palace to their home; then outside talk will cease of itself." That same day the Grand Empress Dowager sent palace envoys to return the two daughters to Min's household.
translations.idiomatic: Liu said, "Only send them back from the Southern Inner Palace to Min's home, and the rumors will die." That same day the grand empress dowager sent envoys to return the two daughters to Min.

sentences.zh: 上好詩，嘗欲置詩學士。

translations.literal: The emperor loved poetry and once wished to establish the office of Poetry Academician.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor loved poetry and once wanted to create a post of poetry academician.

sentences.zh: 李玨曰：「今之詩人浮薄，無益於理。」

translations.literal: Li Jue said: "Today's poets are frivolous; they benefit governance not at all."
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue objected, "Poets today are shallow; they do nothing for statecraft."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon he dropped the plan.
translations.idiomatic: The idea was dropped.

sentences.zh: 甲戌以蔡州刺史韓威爲義武節度使。

translations.literal: On day jiaxu, Han Wei, prefect of Cai, was made military governor of Yiwu.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu day Han Wei, prefect of Cai, was appointed military governor of Yiwu.

sentences.zh: 河東節度使、司徒、中書令裴度以疾求歸東都，十二月，辛丑，詔度入知政事，遣中使敦諭上道。

translations.literal: Pei Du, military governor of Hedong, Grand Preceptor, and Chief Minister of the Secretariat, because of illness asked to return to the eastern capital; twelfth month, day xinchou, an edict ordered Du to enter court to handle administration, and palace envoys were sent to urge him on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du, military governor of Hedong, grand preceptor, and chief minister, asked to retire to Luoyang because of illness. In the twelfth month, on xinchou day, an edict recalled him to take part in government, and envoys were sent to hurry him on his way.

sentences.zh: 鄭覃累表辭位，丙午，詔：三五日一入中書。

translations.literal: Zheng Tan repeatedly memorialized to resign; on day bingwu an edict said he should enter the Secretariat once every three to five days.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tan repeatedly asked to resign; on bingwu day an edict allowed him to attend the Secretariat only every few days.

sentences.zh: 是歳，吐蕃彝泰贊普卒，弟達磨立。

translations.literal: That year the Tibetan ruler Yitai died; his younger brother Damo succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Tibetan ruler Yitai died and his younger brother Damo succeeded.

sentences.zh: 彝泰多病，委政大臣，由是僅能自守，久不爲邊患。

translations.literal: Yitai was often ill and entrusted government to his ministers; therefore he could barely hold his own and for a long time was no border menace.
translations.idiomatic: Yitai had been sickly and left affairs to his ministers, so Tibet barely held together and had not troubled the borders for years.

sentences.zh: 達磨荒淫殘虐，國人不附，災異相繼，吐蕃益衰。

translations.literal: Damo was dissolute, cruel, and tyrannical; the people did not support him; disasters and portents followed one another, and Tibet declined further.
translations.idiomatic: Damo was dissolute and brutal; the people turned against him; omens and disasters piled up, and Tibet weakened further.

sentences.zh: 春，閏正月，己亥，裴度至京師，以疾歸第，不能入見。

translations.literal: Spring, intercalary first month, day jihai: Pei Du reached the capital; because of illness he returned to his residence and could not enter audience.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on jihai day in the intercalary first month, Pei Du reached the capital but was too ill to attend court and went straight home.

sentences.zh: 上勞問賜賚，使者旁午。

translations.literal: The emperor consoled and rewarded him; envoys came in unbroken succession.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent condolences and gifts; envoys arrived in an endless stream.

sentences.zh: 三月，丙戌，薨，謚曰文忠。

translations.literal: Third month, day bingxu: he died; his posthumous title was Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on bingxu day, he died and was given the posthumous name Wenzhong.

sentences.zh: 上怪度無遺表，問其家，得半稿，以儲嗣未定爲憂，言不及私。

translations.literal: The emperor wondered that Du had left no final memorial; when he asked the family they obtained a half-finished draft, anxious that the heir was not settled and speaking nothing of private matters.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was surprised that Du had left no death memorial; the family produced a half-finished draft showing anxiety that the succession was unsettled and saying nothing personal.

sentences.zh: 度身貌不逾中人，而威望遠達四夷。

translations.literal: Du's stature did not exceed that of an ordinary man, yet his prestige reached far into the four barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Du was no taller than an average man, yet his authority reached the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 四夷見唐使，輒問度老少用捨。

translations.literal: Whenever the four barbarians saw a Tang envoy they would ask whether Du was old or young and whether he was employed or dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever foreign envoys met Tang officials they asked whether Pei Du was still young or old and still in or out of office.

sentences.zh: 以身系國家輕重如郭子儀者，二十餘年。

translations.literal: For more than twenty years there was no one who, like Guo Ziyi, bore the state's weight upon his person.
translations.idiomatic: For more than twenty years no one had borne the state's weight on his person as Guo Ziyi had.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，戊辰，上稱判度支杜悰之才，楊嗣復、李玨因請除悰戸部尚書，陳夷行曰：「恩旨當由上出，自古失其國者未始不由權在臣下也。」

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day wuchen: the emperor praised Du Cong's talent as acting head of the treasury; Yang Sifu and Li Jue thereupon asked to appoint Cong Minister of Revenue; Chen Yixing said: "Favor should come from above; from antiquity states have never been lost except when power rested with subjects below."
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on wuchen day in the fourth month, the emperor praised Du Cong, acting head of the treasury. Yang Sifu and Li Jue asked to make him minister of revenue. Chen Yixing objected, "Imperial favor must come from the throne. States are lost when ministers seize power."

sentences.zh: 玨曰：「陛下嘗語臣雲，人主當擇宰相，不當疑宰相。」

translations.literal: Jue said: "Your Majesty once told this subject that a ruler should choose his chief ministers and not suspect them."
translations.idiomatic: Jue said, "Your Majesty once told me that a ruler should choose his ministers and not suspect them."

sentences.zh: 五月，丁亥，上與宰相論政事，陳夷行復言不宜使威權在下，李玨曰：「夷行意疑宰相中有弄陛下威權者耳。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day dinghai: the emperor discussed government with the chief ministers; Chen Yixing again said that awesome power should not rest below; Li Jue said: "Yixing's meaning is to suspect that among the chief ministers there is one who manipulates Your Majesty's authority.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai day in the fifth month the emperor discussed policy with his ministers. Chen Yixing again warned against power below the throne. Li Jue said, "Yixing suspects one of us is manipulating Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 臣屢求退，苟得王傅，臣之幸也。」

translations.literal: This subject has repeatedly asked to retire; if I may have the post of tutor to the heir, it would be this subject's good fortune."
translations.idiomatic: I have asked to resign many times. If I may become tutor to the heir, I would count myself fortunate."

sentences.zh: 鄭覃曰：「陛下開成元年、二年政事殊美，三年、四年漸不如前。」

translations.literal: Zheng Tan said: "In the first and second years of the Kaicheng era Your Majesty's government was especially fine; the third and fourth years have gradually been less so."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tan said, "In Kaicheng one and two your rule was excellent; in three and four it has slipped."

sentences.zh: 楊嗣復曰：「元年、二年鄭覃、夷行用事，三年、四年臣與李玨同之，罪皆在臣！」

translations.literal: Yang Sifu said: "In the first and second years Tan and Yixing held power; in the third and fourth years this subject and Li Jue shared it—the guilt is all mine!"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sifu shot back, "In one and two Tan and Yixing ran things; in three and four Jue and I did. Blame me if you like!"

sentences.zh: 因叩頭曰：「臣不敢更入中書！」

translations.literal: He then kowtowed and said: "This subject dares not enter the Secretariat again!"
translations.idiomatic: He kowtowed and cried, "I dare not enter the Secretariat again!"

sentences.zh: 遂趨出。

translations.literal: And hurried out.
translations.idiomatic: Then he rushed out.

sentences.zh: 上遣中使召還，勞之曰：「鄭覃失言，卿何遽爾！」

translations.literal: The emperor sent a palace envoy to summon him back and comforted him: "Tan spoke rashly—why are you so hasty!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent an envoy to call him back and said, "Tan spoke rashly—why take it so hard?"

sentences.zh: 覃起謝曰：「臣愚拙，意亦不屬嗣復；

translations.literal: Tan rose and apologized: "This subject is dull and clumsy; my meaning was not aimed at Sifu;
translations.idiomatic: Tan rose and apologized, "I spoke clumsily and did not mean Sifu;

sentences.zh: 而遽如是，乃嗣復不容臣耳。」

translations.literal: yet he reacts like this—it is that Sifu will not tolerate this subject."
translations.idiomatic: but he acts like this because Sifu will not tolerate me."

sentences.zh: 嗣復曰：「覃言政事一年不如一年，非獨臣應得罪，亦上累聖德。」

translations.literal: Sifu said: "Tan said government year by year has grown worse—not only should this subject be guilty; it also burdens Your Majesty's sacred virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Sifu said, "Tan said each year the government grows worse. That insults not only me but Your Majesty's virtue."

sentences.zh: 退，三上表辭位，上遣中使召出之，癸巳，始入朝。

translations.literal: He withdrew and thrice memorialized to resign; the emperor sent palace envoys to summon him out; on day guisi he at last entered court.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew and submitted three resignations; the emperor sent envoys to coax him back; on guisi day he finally returned to court.

sentences.zh: 丙申，門下侍郎、同平章事鄭覃罷爲右僕射，陳夷行罷爲吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: On day bingshen, Zheng Tan, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor of the Same Rank, was removed to Right Vice Director; Chen Yixing was removed to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen day Zheng Tan was demoted from co–grand councilor to right vice director, and Chen Yixing to vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 覃性清儉，夷行亦耿介，故嗣復等深疾之。

translations.literal: Tan's nature was pure and frugal; Yixing was also upright; therefore Sifu and the others deeply hated them.
translations.idiomatic: Tan was austere and Yixing rigid; Sifu and his allies hated them deeply.

sentences.zh: 上以鹽鐵推官、檢校禮部員外郎姚勖能鞫疑獄，命權知職方員外郎，右丞韋溫不聽，上奏稱：「郎官朝廷清選，不宜以賞能吏。」

translations.literal: Because Yao Xu, salt-and-iron investigating officer and acting Director of Rites, could try doubtful cases, the emperor ordered him to act as Director of Bureaucratic Appointments; Vice Director Wei Wen would not approve; the emperor memorialized: "Directorate posts are pure selections of the court and should not reward skilled clerks."
translations.idiomatic: “The emperor wanted to promote Yao Xu, a salt-and-iron investigator who excelled at criminal cases, to acting director of bureaucratic appointments, but vice director Wei Wen refused. The emperor argued that court posts should not be rewards for clerical skill.”

sentences.zh: 上乃以勖檢校禮部郎中，依前鹽鐵推官。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon made Xu Acting Director of Rites and left him as before in the salt-and-iron post.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then made Xu acting director of rites while keeping him on the salt-and-iron staff.

sentences.zh: 六月，丁丑，上以其事問宰相楊嗣復，對曰：「溫志在澄清流品。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day dingchou: the emperor asked Chief Minister Yang Sifu about the affair; he replied: "Wen's aim is to clarify the ranks of the pure stream.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou day in the sixth month the emperor asked Yang Sifu about the dispute. Sifu said, "Wen wants to keep the pure stream pure.

sentences.zh: 右有吏能者皆不得清流，則天下之事孰爲陛下理之！

translations.literal: If on the right those with clerical ability may not enter the pure stream, then who under heaven will handle affairs for Your Majesty!
translations.idiomatic: If men of administrative talent cannot join the pure stream, who will run the government for Your Majesty?

sentences.zh: 恐似衰晉之風。」

translations.literal: I fear it resembles the style of declining Jin."
translations.idiomatic: That sounds like the dying days of Jin."

sentences.zh: 然上素重溫，終不奪其所守。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor had long valued Wen and in the end did not override what he upheld.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor respected Wen too much to overrule him.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，癸未，以張元益爲左驍衞將軍，以其母侯莫陳氏爲趙國太夫人，賜絹二百匹。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, day guiwei: Zhang Yuanyi was made General of the Left Valiant Guards; his mother, Lady Houmo Chen, was made Grand Lady of Zhao and given two hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, on guiwei day in the seventh month, Zhang Yuanyi was made general of the Left Valiant Guards; his mother Lady Houmo Chen was made grand lady of Zhao and given two hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 易定之亂，侯莫陳氏説諭將士，且戒元益以順朝命，故賞之。

translations.literal: In the Yiding turmoil Lady Houmo Chen persuaded and admonished the troops and also warned Yuanyi to obey the court's command; therefore she was rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yiding revolt she had persuaded the troops and urged Yuanyi to obey the court, and was rewarded for it.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，以太常卿崔鄲同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: On day jiachen, Cui Lin, Director of Imperial Sacrifices, was made Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery of the Same Rank.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen day Cui Lin, director of imperial sacrifices, was made grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 鄲，郾之弟也。

translations.literal: Lin was the younger brother of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Lin was the younger brother of Cui Yan.

sentences.zh: 八月，辛亥，鄜王憬薨。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day xinhai: Prince of Bin Yun died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on xinhai day, Prince of Bin Yun died.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，昭義節度使劉從諫上言：「蕭本詐稱太后弟，上下皆稱蕭弘是真，以本來自左軍，故弘爲台司所抑。

translations.literal: On day guiyou, Liu Congjian, military governor of Zhaoyi, memorialized: "Xiao Ben falsely claimed to be the empress dowager's younger brother; above and below all call Xiao Hong the true one, yet because Ben came from the Left Army, Hong was suppressed by the censorate.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou day Liu Congjian, military governor of Zhaoyi, wrote, "Xiao Ben falsely claimed to be the empress dowager's brother. Everyone says Xiao Hong is genuine, but because Ben came from the Left Army, Hong was blocked by the censorate.

sentences.zh: 今弘詣臣，求臣上聞。

translations.literal: Now Hong has come to this subject and asks this subject to report upward.
translations.idiomatic: Now Hong has come to me and asks me to report to the throne.

sentences.zh: 乞追弘赴闕，與本對推，以正真偽。」

translations.literal: I beg that Hong be summoned to court to confront Ben and determine truth from falsehood."
translations.idiomatic: Summon Hong to court and confront him with Ben to settle who is real."

sentences.zh: 詔三司鞫之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the three judicial offices to try the case.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered the three judicial offices to investigate.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，乙卯，上就起居舍人魏謨取記注觀之，謨不可，曰：「記注兼書善惡，所以儆戒入君。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day yimao: the emperor asked Wei Mo, Gentleman of the Imperial Diary, to hand over the record for him to read; Mo refused, saying: "The record records both good and evil in order to warn and admonish the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, on yimao day in the tenth month, the emperor asked Wei Mo for the imperial diary to read. Mo refused, saying, "The diary records good and evil alike to warn the ruler.

sentences.zh: 陛下但力爲善，不必觀史！」

translations.literal: Your Majesty need only strive to do good; you need not read the history!"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should simply do good—you need not read the history!"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕向嘗觀之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I have read it before."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I have read it before."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「此曏日史官之罪也。

translations.literal: He replied: "That was the fault of the historians of former days.
translations.idiomatic: Mo replied, "That was the fault of earlier historians.

sentences.zh: 若陛下自觀史，則史官必有所諱避，何以取信於後！」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty reads the history yourself, the historians will certainly hedge and avoid; how can later ages trust it!"
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty reads it, historians will flatter you—how will posterity trust the record?"

sentences.zh: 上乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave up the idea.

sentences.zh: 楊妃請立皇弟安王溶爲嗣，上謀於宰相，李玨非之。

translations.literal: Consort Yang asked to establish the emperor's younger brother, Prince of An Rong, as heir; the emperor consulted the chief ministers, and Li Jue opposed it.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Yang wanted Prince of An Rong installed as heir; the emperor consulted his ministers, and Li Jue objected.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，立敬宗少子陳王成美爲皇太子。

translations.literal: On day bingyin, the emperor's younger son by Emperor Jingzong, Prince of Chen Chengmei, was established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin day Prince of Chen Chengmei, a younger son of Emperor Jingzong, was named crown prince.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，上幸會寧殿作樂，有童子緣橦，一夫來往走其下如狂。

translations.literal: On day dingmao the emperor visited the Hall of Tranquil Union for music; a boy was on a pole; a man ran back and forth beneath it like a madman.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao day the emperor watched music at the Hall of Tranquil Union. A boy performed on a pole while a man ran beneath him as if crazed.

sentences.zh: 上怪之，左右曰：「其父也。」

translations.literal: The emperor was astonished; attendants said: "That is his father."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was startled. Attendants said, "That is his father."

sentences.zh: 上泫然流涕曰：「朕貴爲天子，不能全一子。」

translations.literal: The emperor wept and said: "I am exalted as Son of Heaven yet cannot save one son."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept and said, "I am emperor yet I could not save even one son."

sentences.zh: 召教坊劉楚材等四人、宮人張十十等十人，責之曰：「構害太子，皆爾曹也！

translations.literal: He summoned Liu Chucai and three others of the Music Bureau and Zhang Shishi and nine other palace women and rebuked them: "You are the ones who plotted harm to the crown prince!
translations.idiomatic: He summoned four musicians of the Music Bureau and ten palace women and accused them, "You destroyed the crown prince!

sentences.zh: 今更立太子，復欲爾邪？」

translations.literal: Now that a new crown prince is established, do you wish to do it again?"
translations.idiomatic: Do you mean to do the same to the new heir?"

sentences.zh: 執以付吏，己巳，皆殺之。

translations.literal: They were seized and handed to the law officers; on day jisi all were executed.
translations.idiomatic: They were handed to the law officers, and on jisi day all were killed.

sentences.zh: 上因是感傷，舊疾遂增。

translations.literal: Because of this the emperor was moved to grief and his old illness grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: Grief worsened his old illness.

sentences.zh: 十一月，三司案蕭本、蕭弘皆非真太后弟。

translations.literal: Eleventh month: the three judicial offices judged that neither Xiao Ben nor Xiao Hong was the empress dowager's true younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the three offices ruled that neither Xiao Ben nor Xiao Hong was the empress dowager's real brother.

sentences.zh: 本除名，流愛州，弘流儋州。

translations.literal: Ben was stripped of name and exiled to Aizhou; Hong was exiled to Danzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ben was disgraced and exiled to Aizhou; Hong to Danzhou.

sentences.zh: 而太后真弟在閔中，終不能自達。

translations.literal: Yet the empress dowager's true younger brother was in Min and could never make himself known.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager's real brother lived in Fujian and never reached the court.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，上疾少間，坐思政殿，召當直學士周墀，賜之酒，因問曰：「朕可方前代何主？」

translations.literal: On day yihai the emperor's illness eased slightly; he sat in the Hall of Governance and summoned the duty academician Zhou Chi, gave him wine, and asked: "With which ruler of former ages may I be compared?"
translations.idiomatic: On yihai day, when his illness briefly eased, the emperor sat in the Hall of Governance, summoned duty academician Zhou Chi, gave him wine, and asked, "Which ruler of old am I like?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下堯、舜之主也。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Your Majesty is a ruler of the caliber of Yao and Shun."
translations.idiomatic: Chi answered, "Your Majesty is a Yao or Shun."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕豈敢比堯、舜！

translations.literal: The emperor said: "How dare I compare myself to Yao and Shun!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "How dare I compare myself to Yao and Shun!

sentences.zh: 所以問卿者，何如周赧、漢獻耳。」

translations.literal: What I asked you is whether I am like King Nan of Zhou or Emperor Xian of Han."
translations.idiomatic: I meant—am I like King Nan of Zhou or Emperor Xian of Han?"

sentences.zh: 墀驚曰：「彼亡國之主，豈可比聖德！」

translations.literal: Chi was alarmed and said: "Those were rulers of perished states—how can they be compared to Your Majesty's sacred virtue!"
translations.idiomatic: Chi was shocked. "Those were doomed rulers—how can they compare to Your Majesty?"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「赧、獻受制於強諸侯，今朕受制於家奴，以此言之，朕殆不如！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Nan and Xian were controlled by powerful feudal lords; now I am controlled by household slaves—in this respect I am perhaps not their equal!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Nan and Xian were controlled by powerful lords. I am controlled by household slaves. In that respect I am worse than they!"

sentences.zh: 因泣下沾襟，墀伏地流涕，自是不復視朝。

translations.literal: He wept until his robe was soaked; Chi lay prostrate weeping; from then on he no longer held court.
translations.idiomatic: Tears soaked his robe; Chi lay weeping on the floor. The emperor never held court again.

sentences.zh: 是歳，天下戸口四百九十九萬六千七百五十二。

translations.literal: That year the empire's registered households numbered 4,996,752.
translations.idiomatic: That year registered households in the empire totaled 4,996,752.

sentences.zh: 回鶻相安允合、特勒柴革謀作亂，彰信可汗殺之。

translations.literal: The Uighur chancellor An Yunhe and the tele Tiele Chaige plotted rebellion; the Zhenxin qaghan killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Uighur chancellor An Yunhe and tele Tiele Chaige plotted rebellion; the Zhenxin qaghan had them killed.

sentences.zh: 相掘羅勿將兵在外，以馬三百賂沙陀朱邪赤心，借其兵共攻可汗。

translations.literal: Chancellor Juoluowu commanded troops outside; with three hundred horses he bribed the Shatuo Zhuye Chixin to borrow troops and jointly attack the qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Juoluowu, commanding troops abroad, bribed the Shatuo leader Zhuye Chixin with three hundred horses for help attacking the qaghan.

sentences.zh: 可汗兵敗，自殺，國人立馺特勒爲可汗。

translations.literal: The qaghan's army was defeated; he killed himself; the people installed Tele Facha as qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: The qaghan's army was defeated and he killed himself; the people installed Facha as qaghan.

sentences.zh: 會歳疫，大雪，羊、馬多死，回鶻遂衰。

translations.literal: Just then plague came and heavy snow fell; many sheep and horses died, and the Uighurs declined further.
translations.idiomatic: Plague and heavy snow killed many herds, and the Uighurs weakened further.

sentences.zh: 赤心，執宜之子也。

translations.literal: Chixin was the son of Zhiyi.
translations.idiomatic: Chixin was the son of Zhuye Zhiyi.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，己卯，詔立穎王瀍爲皇太弟，應軍國事權令句當。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, day jimao: an edict established Prince of Ying Chan as imperial younger brother and ordered him to take charge of military and state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on jimao day in the first month, an edict made Prince of Ying Chan imperial younger brother with charge of military and state affairs.

sentences.zh: 且言太子成美年尚沖幼，未漸師資，可復封陳王。

translations.literal: It also said Crown Prince Chengmei was still young and had not yet received tutors and could again be enfeoffed as Prince of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: It said Crown Prince Chengmei was still young and untutored and could be re-enfeoffed as Prince of Chen.

sentences.zh: 時上疾甚，命知樞密劉弘逸、薛季陵引楊嗣復、李玨至禁中，欲奉太子監國。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor was gravely ill; he ordered Liu Hongyi and Xue Jiling of the Bureau of Military Affairs to bring Yang Sifu and Li Jue into the inner palace, intending to have the crown prince oversee the state.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was gravely ill and ordered Liu Hongyi and Xue Jiling to bring Yang Sifu and Li Jue into the palace so the crown prince could oversee the state.

sentences.zh: 中尉仇士良、魚弘志以太子之立，功不在己，乃言太子幼，且有疾，更議所立。

translations.literal: Chief Commandant Qiu Shiliang and Yu Hongzhi, because the crown prince's establishment owed nothing to them, said the crown prince was young and also ill and that another choice should be discussed.
translations.idiomatic: Chief commandants Qiu Shiliang and Yu Hongzhi, who had gained nothing from the crown prince's appointment, said he was young and sick and another heir should be chosen.

sentences.zh: 李玨曰：「太子位已定，豈得中變！」

translations.literal: Li Jue said: "The crown prince's place is already fixed—how can it be changed midway!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue said, "The heir is already chosen—how can you change him now?"

sentences.zh: 士良、弘志遂矯詔立瀍爲太弟。

translations.literal: Shiliang and Hongzhi thereupon forged an edict establishing Chan as imperial younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang and Hongzhi forged an edict making Chan imperial younger brother instead.

sentences.zh: 是日，士良、弘志將兵詣十六宅，迎穎王至少陽院，百官謁見于思賢殿。

translations.literal: That day Shiliang and Hongzhi led troops to the sixteen princely residences, escorted the Prince of Ying to the Shaoyang Quarter, and the hundred officials paid homage at the Hall of Worthy Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: That day they led troops to the princes' quarters, brought the Prince of Ying to Shaoyang, and officials paid homage at the Hall of Worthy Counsel.

sentences.zh: 瀍沉毅有斷，喜慍不形於色。

translations.literal: Chan was deep, resolute, and decisive; joy and anger did not show on his face.
translations.idiomatic: Chan was deep, resolute, and inscrutable.

sentences.zh: 與安王溶皆素爲上所厚，異於諸王。

translations.literal: He and Prince of An Rong had both long been favored by the emperor above the other princes.
translations.idiomatic: He and Prince of An Rong had long been the emperor's favorites among the princes.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，上崩於太和殿。

translations.literal: On day xinsi the emperor died in the Hall of Grand Harmony.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi day the emperor died in the Hall of Grand Harmony.

sentences.zh: 以楊嗣復攝塚宰。

translations.literal: Yang Sifu was ordered to act as chief mourner.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sifu was named acting chief mourner.

sentences.zh: 癸未，仇士良説太弟賜楊賢妃、安王溶、陳王成美死。

translations.literal: On day guiwei, Qiu Shiliang persuaded the imperial younger brother to grant death to Worthy Consort Yang, Prince of An Rong, and Prince of Chen Chengmei.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei day Shiliang persuaded the new ruler to execute Worthy Consort Yang and Princes Rong and Chengmei.

sentences.zh: 敕大行以十四日殯，成服。

translations.literal: An edict for the late emperor set the fourteenth day for encoffining and donning mourning.
translations.idiomatic: An edict set the fourteenth day for encoffining the late emperor.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫裴夷直上言期日太遠，不聽。

translations.literal: Remonstrating Censor Pei Yizhi memorialized that the date was too distant; it was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Pei Yizhi said the date was too far off; he was ignored.

sentences.zh: 時仇士良等追怨文宗，凡樂工及內侍得幸於文宗者，誅貶相繼。

translations.literal: At the time Shiliang and the others, pursuing old resentment against Wenzong, executed or demoted in succession every musician and inner attendant who had won Wenzong's favor.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang and his allies now hunted down every musician and eunuch Wenzong had favored.

sentences.zh: 夷直復上言：「陛下自籓維繼統，是宜儼然在疚，以哀慕爲心，速行喪禮，早議大政，以慰天下。

translations.literal: Yizhi again memorialized: "Since Your Majesty succeeded from a princely establishment, you should solemnly observe mourning, take grief and longing as your heart, hasten the funeral rites, and early deliberate great affairs to comfort the empire.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi memorialized again, "Your Majesty succeeded from a princely estate. You should mourn properly, hurry the funeral, and take up government soon to comfort the realm.

sentences.zh: 而未及數日，屢誅戮先帝近臣，驚率土之視聽，傷先帝之神靈，人情何瞻！

translations.literal: Yet before several days had passed he repeatedly executed the late emperor's close attendants, startling the empire's eyes and ears and wounding the late emperor's spirit—how can the people's feelings look upward!
translations.idiomatic: Yet within days he executed Wenzong's closest attendants, shocking the realm, wounding Wenzong's spirit, and leaving the people nowhere to turn their gaze.

sentences.zh: 國體至重，若使此輩無罪，固不可刑；

translations.literal: The state's body is supremely weighty: if these men are without guilt, they certainly should not be punished;
translations.idiomatic: The dignity of the state is at stake. If they are innocent, they must not be punished;

sentences.zh: 若其有罪，彼已在天網之內，無所逃伏，旬日之外行之何晩！」

translations.literal: if they are guilty, they are already within heaven's net and cannot escape; to act ten days hence—how would that be late!"
translations.idiomatic: if they are guilty, they are already in heaven's net. Waiting ten days would change nothing."

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: It was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，文宗始大斂。

translations.literal: On day xinmao the encoffining of Wenzong began in earnest.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao day Wenzong's body was formally encoffined.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位。

translations.literal: Wuzong took the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 甲午，追尊上母韋妃爲皇太后。

translations.literal: On day jiawu the emperor's mother, Consort Wei, was posthumously honored as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu day the new emperor's mother, Consort Wei, was honored as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 二月，乙卯，赦天下。

translations.literal: Second month, day yimao: a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on yimao day, the empire was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，謚韋太后曰宣懿。

translations.literal: On day bingyin the posthumous title of Empress Dowager Wei was fixed as Xuanyi.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin day Empress Dowager Wei was given the temple name Xuanyi.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，己卯，門下侍郎、同平章事楊嗣復罷爲吏部尚書，以刑部尚書崔珙同平章事兼鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: Summer, fifth month, day jimao: Yang Sifu, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor of the Same Rank, was removed to Minister of Personnel; Cui Gong, Minister of Punishments, was made Grand Councilor of the Same Rank and Commissioner of Salt and Iron Transport.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on jimao day in the fifth month, Yang Sifu was demoted to minister of personnel and Cui Gong, minister of punishments, was made co–grand councilor and salt-and-iron commissioner.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，壬戌，葬元聖昭獻孝皇帝於章陵，廟號文宗。

translations.literal: Autumn, eighth month, day renxu: the Yuan Sage, Illustrious Offerer, Filial Emperor was buried at Zhangling; his temple name was Wenzong.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, on renxu day in the eighth month, Wenzong was buried at Zhangling.

sentences.zh: 庚午，門下侍郎、同平章事李玨坐爲山陵使龍輴陷，罷爲太常卿。

translations.literal: On day gengwu, Li Jue, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor of the Same Rank, because as commissioner for the imperial tomb the dragon carriage sank, was removed to Director of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu day Li Jue was demoted to director of imperial sacrifices because the imperial hearse sank while he oversaw Wenzong's tomb.

sentences.zh: 貶京兆尹敬昕爲郴州司馬。

translations.literal: Jingzhao Prefect Jing Xin was demoted to vice prefect of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhao prefect Jing Xin was demoted to vice prefect of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 義武軍亂，逐節度使陳君賞。

translations.literal: The Yiwu army mutinied and drove out Military Governor Chen Junshang.
translations.idiomatic: The Yiwu garrison mutinied and expelled military governor Chen Junshang.

sentences.zh: 君賞募勇士數百，復入軍城，誅亂者。

translations.literal: Junshang recruited several hundred warriors, re-entered the army city, and executed the mutineers.
translations.idiomatic: Junshang raised several hundred warriors, re-entered the garrison city, and killed the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 初，上之立非宰相意，故楊嗣復、李玨相繼罷去，召淮南節度使李德裕入朝。

translations.literal: Earlier, the emperor's enthronement had not been the chief ministers' wish; therefore Yang Sifu and Li Jue were removed in succession, and Li Deyu, military governor of Huainan, was summoned to court.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong's accession had not been the ministers' plan, so Yang Sifu and Li Jue were dismissed and Li Deyu was recalled from Huainan.

sentences.zh: 九月，甲戌朔，至京師。

translations.literal: Ninth month, first day jiaxu: he reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the first day of the month, he reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，以德裕爲門下侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: On day dingchou, Deyu was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor of the Same Rank.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou day Deyu was made vice director of the Secretariat and co–grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，德裕入謝，言於上曰：「致理之要，在於辯群臣之邪正。

translations.literal: On day gengchen, Deyu entered to give thanks and said to the emperor: "The key to good order lies in distinguishing the upright from the depraved among the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen day Deyu thanked the emperor and said, "Good government depends on telling loyal ministers from corrupt ones.

sentences.zh: 夫邪正二者，勢不相容。

translations.literal: The upright and the depraved—these two cannot stand together.
translations.idiomatic: The two cannot coexist.

sentences.zh: 正人指邪人爲邪，邪人亦指正人爲邪，人主辯之甚難。

translations.literal: The upright point to the depraved as depraved; the depraved also point to the upright as depraved; for the ruler to distinguish them is very difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Each calls the other wicked, and the ruler's task is hard.

sentences.zh: 臣以爲正人如松柏，特立不倚；

translations.literal: This subject considers the upright like pine and cypress, standing alone without leaning;
translations.idiomatic: Upright men are like pine and cypress, standing alone;

sentences.zh: 邪人如籐蘿，非附他物不能自起。

translations.literal: the depraved like vines and creepers, unable to rise unless they cling to something else.
translations.idiomatic: wicked men are like vines that cannot rise without clinging to something else.

sentences.zh: 故正人一心事君，而邪人競爲朋黨。

translations.literal: Therefore the upright serve the ruler with one heart, while the depraved compete to form factions.
translations.idiomatic: Upright men serve the throne wholeheartedly; wicked men form factions.

sentences.zh: 先帝深知朋黨之患，然所用卒皆朋黨之人，良由執心不定，故奸邪得乘間而入也。

translations.literal: The late emperor deeply knew the harm of factions, yet those he finally employed were all faction men—truly because his resolve was unsteady, so the wicked could slip in between.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong knew the harm of factions yet ended up employing faction men because his resolve wavered and the wicked slipped in.

sentences.zh: 夫宰相不能人人忠良，或爲欺罔。

translations.literal: Chief ministers cannot all be loyal; some may deceive.
translations.idiomatic: Not every minister is loyal; some deceive.

sentences.zh: 主心始疑，於是旁詢小臣以察執政。

translations.literal: When the ruler's heart first grows suspicious, he then asks petty officials beside him to examine those in power.
translations.idiomatic: Once the ruler grows suspicious he consults petty officials about his ministers.

sentences.zh: 如德宗末年，所聽任者惟裴延齡輩，宰相署敕而已，此政事所以日亂也。

translations.literal: Like the last years of Dezong, when those he listened to were only Pei Yanling and his sort while the chief ministers merely countersigned edicts—this is why government daily grew chaotic.
translations.idiomatic: Like Dezong's last years, when he listened only to flatterers while ministers merely countersigned—that is how government decays.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠能慎擇賢才以爲宰相，有奸罔者立黜去之，常令政事皆出中書，推心委任，堅定不移，則天下何憂不理哉！」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty can carefully choose worthy talent as chief ministers, immediately dismiss any who deceive, always let government come from the Secretariat, give your heart and trust without wavering, then what worry is there that the empire will not be well governed!"
translations.idiomatic: Choose worthy ministers, dismiss deceivers at once, keep government in the Secretariat, and trust your ministers firmly—the realm will govern itself."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「先帝於大臣好爲形跡，小過皆含容不言，日累月積，以至禍敗。

translations.literal: He also said: "The late emperor with his great ministers liked to track their traces; small faults he would cover and not speak of; day piled on month until disaster came.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Wenzong noted his ministers' every move, swallowed small faults in silence, and piled up resentment until disaster struck.

sentences.zh: 茲事大誤，願陛下以爲戒！

translations.literal: This matter was a great error; I wish Your Majesty to take it as a warning!
translations.idiomatic: That was a grave mistake. Your Majesty must avoid it!

sentences.zh: 臣等有罪，陛下當面詰之。

translations.literal: When this subject and others are guilty, Your Majesty should question us to our faces.
translations.idiomatic: When we are accused, question us to our faces.

sentences.zh: 事苟無實，得以辯明；

translations.literal: If the affair has no substance, we can clarify it;
translations.idiomatic: If the charge is false, we can answer it;

sentences.zh: 若其有實，辭理自窮。

translations.literal: if it has substance, our arguments will naturally be exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: if it is true, we will have no defense.

sentences.zh: 小過則容其悛改，大罪則加之誅遣，如此，君臣之際無疑間矣。」

translations.literal: Small faults—allow amendment; great crimes—add execution and banishment; thus between ruler and minister there will be no suspicion."
translations.idiomatic: Pardon small faults and punish great crimes openly—then ruler and minister will trust one another."

sentences.zh: 上嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 初，德裕在淮南，敕召監軍楊欽義。

translations.literal: Earlier, while Deyu was in Huainan, an edict summoned Army Supervisor Yang Qinyi.
translations.idiomatic: While Deyu was in Huainan, the court summoned army supervisor Yang Qinyi.

sentences.zh: 人皆言必知樞密，德裕待之無加禮，欽義心銜之。

translations.literal: Everyone said he would certainly know military affairs at the Bureau; Deyu treated him without added ceremony, and Qinyi bore a grudge in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone assumed he would join the Bureau of Military Affairs; Deyu treated him casually, and Qinyi resented it.

sentences.zh: 一旦，獨延欽義，置酒中堂，情禮極厚。

translations.literal: One day he received Qinyi alone, set wine in the central hall, and showed extreme courtesy and affection.
translations.idiomatic: One day Deyu entertained Qinyi alone in the central hall with exceptional courtesy.

sentences.zh: 陳珍玩數床，罷酒，皆以贈之，欽義大喜過望。

translations.literal: Several beds of rare objects were set out; when the wine ended, all were given to him; Qinyi was delighted beyond expectation.
translations.idiomatic: He displayed rare treasures and gave them all to Qinyi when the banquet ended. Qinyi was astonished.

sentences.zh: 行至汴州，敕復還淮南，欽義盡以所餉歸之。

translations.literal: When he reached Bianzhou an edict sent him back to Huainan; Qinyi returned everything he had been given.
translations.idiomatic: At Bianzhou an edict sent him back to Huainan, and he returned the gifts.

sentences.zh: 德裕曰：「此何直！」

translations.literal: Deyu said: "What is this worth!"
translations.idiomatic: Deyu said, "Keep them—they are nothing."

sentences.zh: 卒以與之。

translations.literal: In the end he gave them to him.
translations.idiomatic: He insisted Qinyi keep them.

sentences.zh: 其後欽義竟知樞密；

translations.literal: Afterward Qinyi did indeed know military affairs at the Bureau;
translations.idiomatic: Qinyi did become director of the Bureau of Military Affairs;

sentences.zh: 德裕柄用，欽義頗有力焉。

translations.literal: when Deyu held power, Qinyi was quite influential.
translations.idiomatic: and when Deyu held power, Qinyi helped him greatly.

sentences.zh: 初，伊吾之西，焉耆之北，有黠戛斯部落，即古之堅昆，唐初結骨也，後更號黠戛斯。

translations.literal: Earlier, west of Yiwu and north of Yanqi, there was the Kirghiz tribe—the ancient Jiankun, Jiegu in early Tang, later renamed Kirghiz.
translations.idiomatic: West of Yiwu and north of Yanqi lived the Kirghiz—the ancient Jiankun, called Jiegu in early Tang, later Kirghiz.

sentences.zh: 乾元中爲回鶻所破，自是隔閡不通中國。

translations.literal: In the Qianyuan era they were broken by the Uighurs; from then on they were cut off from China.
translations.idiomatic: The Uighurs defeated them in the Qianyuan era, and contact with China ceased.

sentences.zh: 其君長曰阿熱，建牙青山，去回鶻牙，橐駝行四十日。

translations.literal: Their chieftain was called A-re; he set his headquarters at Green Mountain, forty days' camel travel from the Uighur headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Their leader A-re established his headquarters at Green Mountain, forty days' camel march from the Uighur capital.

sentences.zh: 其人悍勇，吐蕃、回鶻常賂遺之，假以官號。

translations.literal: These people were fierce and brave; Tibet and the Uighurs often bribed them and lent them titles.
translations.idiomatic: They were fierce warriors; Tibet and the Uighurs bribed them with titles.

sentences.zh: 回鶻既衰，阿熱始自稱可汗。

translations.literal: After the Uighurs declined, A-re first styled himself qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Uighurs weakened, A-re proclaimed himself qaghan.

sentences.zh: 回鶻遣相國將兵擊之，連兵二十餘年，數爲黠戛斯所敗，詈回鶻曰：「汝運盡矣，我必取汝金帳！」

translations.literal: The Uighurs sent their chancellor with troops to attack; for more than twenty years they fought and were several times defeated by the Kirghiz, who reviled the Uighurs: "Your fortune is exhausted; I shall surely take your Golden Tent!"
translations.idiomatic: The Uighurs sent their chancellor against them. For twenty years the Kirghiz beat them and taunted them: "Your luck is spent—I will take your Golden Tent!"

sentences.zh: 金帳者，回鶻可汗所居帳也。

translations.literal: The Golden Tent was the tent where the Uighur qaghan dwelt.
translations.idiomatic: The Golden Tent was the qaghan's dwelling.

sentences.zh: 及掘羅勿殺彰信可汗，立馺，回鶻別將句録莫賀引黠戛斯十萬騎攻回鶻，大破之，殺馺及掘羅勿，焚其牙帳蕩盡，回鶻諸部逃散。

translations.literal: When Juoluowu killed the Zhenxin qaghan and installed Facha, another Uighur general, Juluomohe, led a hundred thousand Kirghiz horsemen to attack the Uighurs, routed them utterly, killed Facha and Juoluowu, burned their headquarters to the ground, and the Uighur tribes scattered.
translations.idiomatic: When Juoluowu killed the qaghan and installed Facha, General Juluomohe led a hundred thousand Kirghiz horsemen, crushed the Uighurs, killed Facha and Juoluowu, burned their capital, and the tribes fled.

sentences.zh: 其相馺職、特勒厖等址五部西奔葛邏祿，一支奔吐蕃，一支奔安西，可汗兄弟嗢沒斯等及其相赤心、僕固、特勒那頡啜各帥其眾抵天德塞下，就雜虜貿易谷食，且求內附。

translations.literal: Chancellor Sazhi, tele Pang, and others of five tribes fled west to the Geluolu; one branch fled to Tibet, one to Anxi; the qaghan's brothers Wumosi and others, with chancellors Chixin, Pugu, and tele Neixiechuo, each led their followers to the Tiande frontier, traded grain with border peoples, and sought to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Sazhi and tele Pang led five tribes west to the Geluolu; others fled to Tibet or Anxi; the qaghan's brothers Wumosi and chancellors Chixin and Pugu led their people to Tiande, traded for grain, and asked to submit.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丙辰，天德軍使溫德彝奏：「回鶻潰兵侵逼西城，亙六十里，不見其後。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day bingchen: Tiande Army Commissioner Wen Deyi memorialized: "Uighur broken troops press the western city for sixty li without end in sight.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, on bingchen day in the tenth month, Tiande commissioner Wen Deyi reported, "Broken Uighur forces press the western frontier for sixty li with no end in sight.

sentences.zh: 邊人以回鶻猥至，恐懼不安。」

translations.literal: Border people, because the Uighurs have come in swarms, fear and are uneasy."
translations.idiomatic: Border people are terrified by the Uighur influx."

sentences.zh: 詔振武節度使劉沔屯雲迦關以備之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Zhenwu Military Governor Liu Mian to encamp at Yunguan Pass to guard against them.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Liu Mian of Zhenwu to guard Yunguan Pass.

sentences.zh: 魏博節度使何進滔薨，軍中推其子都知兵馬使重順知留後。

translations.literal: He Jintao, military governor of Weibo, died; the army pushed his son, Commander of the Army He Zhongshun, to act as acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Weibo military governor He Jintao died; the troops made his son Zhongshun acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 蕭太后徙居興慶宮積慶殿，號積慶太后。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Xiao moved to the Hall of Accumulated Blessings in the Palace of Rising Celebration and was styled Empress Dowager of Accumulated Blessings.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Xiao moved to the Hall of Accumulated Blessings and took the title Accumulated Blessings Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 十一月，癸酉朔，上幸雲陽校獵。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, first day guiyou: the emperor visited Yunyang for a hunting review.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou day, the first of the eleventh month, the emperor hunted at Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 故事，新天子即位，兩省官同署名。

translations.literal: By precedent, when a new Son of Heaven took the throne, officials of both secretariats signed together.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent both secretariats countersigned when a new emperor took the throne.

sentences.zh: 上之即位也，諫議大夫裴夷直漏名，由是出爲杭州刺史。
