translations.literal: At this emperor's accession, Remonstrating Censor Pei Yizhi omitted his signature and was therefore sent out as prefect of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At Wuzong's accession Pei Yizhi omitted his signature and was sent out as prefect of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 開府儀同三司、左衞上將軍兼內謁者監仇士良，請以開府廕其子爲千牛，給事中李中敏判云：「開府階誠宜廕子，謁者監何由有兒？」

translations.literal: Qiu Shiliang, Grand Master of Glorious Ceremony with First Rank, Left Guard Senior General and concurrent Director of Palace Attendants, asked to use his opening-of-office privilege to enfeoff his son as Thousand Bull, Supervising Secretary Li Zhongmin ruled: "Opening-of-office rank may indeed enfeoff a son, but how can a Director of Palace Attendants have a son?"
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Shiliang asked to use his honors to make his son a Thousand-Bull guardsman. Li Zhongmin ruled, "Honors may enfeoff a son, but how can a palace attendant have one?"

sentences.zh: 士良慚恚。

translations.literal: Shiliang was ashamed and resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang was humiliated and furious.

sentences.zh: 李德裕亦以中敏爲楊嗣復之黨，惡之，出爲婺州刺史。

translations.literal: Li Deyu also considered Zhongmin a partisan of Yang Sifu, hated him, and sent him out as prefect of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu thought Zhongmin a partisan of Yang Sifu and sent him out as prefect of Wu.

sentences.zh: 十二月，庚申，以何重順知魏博留後事。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day gengshen: He Zhongshun was made acting commissioner of Weibo.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen day in the twelfth month Zhongshun was confirmed as acting Weibo commissioner.

sentences.zh: 立皇子峻爲杞王。

translations.literal: The emperor's son Jun was established as Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jun was enfeoffed as Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 武宗至道昭肅孝皇帝上

translations.literal: Emperor Wuzong Zhidao Zhaosu Xiaohuangdi, Part One
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wuzong Zhidao Zhaosu Xiaohuangdi, Part One

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛巳，上祀圓丘，赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, day xinsi: the emperor sacrificed at the Round Mound, proclaimed an amnesty, and changed the era name.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on xinsi day in the first month, the emperor sacrificed at the Round Mound, pardoned the empire, and changed the era name.

sentences.zh: 劉沔奏回鶻已退，詔沔還鎮。

translations.literal: Liu Mian memorialized that the Uighurs had withdrawn; an edict ordered Mian to return to his command.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mian reported the Uighurs had withdrawn and was ordered back to his post.

sentences.zh: 二月，回鶻十三部近牙帳者立烏希特勒爲烏介可汗，南保錯子山。

translations.literal: Second month: thirteen Uighur tribes near the headquarters installed Wuhuile as Wujie qaghan and moved south to guard Cuozishan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month thirteen Uighur tribes near the old capital installed Wuhuile as Wujie qaghan and withdrew south to Cuozishan.

sentences.zh: 三月，甲戌，以御史大夫陳夷行爲門下侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: Third month, day jiaxu: Chen Yixing, Censor-in-Chief, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor of the Same Rank.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu day in the third month Chen Yixing was made vice director of the Secretariat and co–grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 初，知樞密劉弘逸、薛季陵寵於文宗，仇士良惡之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Liu Hongyi and Xue Jiling of the Bureau of Military Affairs had been favored by Wenzong; Qiu Shiliang hated them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hongyi and Xue Jiling of the Bureau of Military Affairs had been Wenzong's favorites; Shiliang hated them.

sentences.zh: 上之立，非二人及宰相意，故楊嗣復出爲湖南觀察使，李玨出爲桂管觀察使。

translations.literal: The emperor's enthronement had not been their wish nor the chief ministers'; therefore Yang Sifu was sent out as Observation Commissioner of Hunan and Li Jue as Observation Commissioner of Guiguan.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong's accession had not been their doing, so Yang Sifu was sent to Hunan and Li Jue to Guiguan.

sentences.zh: 士良屢譖弘逸等於上，勸上除之。

translations.literal: Shiliang repeatedly slandered Hongyi and the others to the emperor and urged him to eliminate them.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang repeatedly slandered them and urged the emperor to kill them.

sentences.zh: 乙未，賜弘逸、季陵死，遣中使就潭、桂州誅嗣復及玨。

translations.literal: On day yiwei, Hongyi and Jiling were granted death; palace envoys were sent to Tan and Gui prefectures to execute Sifu and Jue.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei day Hongyi and Jiling were executed; envoys were sent to kill Sifu and Jue in exile.

sentences.zh: 戸部尚書杜悰奔馬見李德裕曰：「天子年少，新即位，茲事不宜手滑！」

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Du Cong ran his horse to see Li Deyu and said: "The Son of Heaven is young and newly enthroned; in this matter he must not act rashly!"
translations.idiomatic: Du Cong galloped to Deyu and said, "The emperor is young and new to the throne—he must not act rashly in this!"

sentences.zh: 丙申，德裕與崔珙、崔鄲、陳夷行三上奏，又邀樞密使至中書，使入奏。

translations.literal: On day bingshen, Deyu with Cui Gong, Cui Lin, and Chen Yixing thrice submitted memorials and also invited the military affairs commissioners to the Secretariat to enter and memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen day Deyu, Cui Gong, Cui Lin, and Chen Yixing submitted three joint memorials and brought military commissioners to the Secretariat to appeal.

sentences.zh: 以爲：「德宗疑劉晏動搖東宮而殺之，中外鹹以爲冤，兩河不臣者由茲恐懼，得以爲辭。

translations.literal: They argued: "Dezong suspected Liu Yan of moving against the eastern palace and killed him; within and without all considered it injustice; the two Hebei circuits that would not submit took this as fear and used it as a pretext.
translations.idiomatic: “They argued that Dezong had killed Liu Yan on suspicion and the empire had called it unjust, giving the Hebei rebels an excuse.

sentences.zh: 德宗後悔，録其子孫。

translations.literal: Dezong later regretted it and enfeoffed his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong later regretted it and honored Yan's descendants.

sentences.zh: 文宗疑宋申錫交通籓邸，竄謫至死。

translations.literal: Wenzong suspected Song Shenxi of communicating with princely establishments and banished him until death.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong suspected Song Shenxi of plotting with princes and exiled him to his death.

sentences.zh: 既而追悔，爲之出涕。

translations.literal: Afterward he repented and wept for it.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong later wept with regret.

sentences.zh: 嗣復、玨等若有罪惡，乞更加重貶。

translations.literal: If Sifu and Jue have crimes, we beg that heavier demotion be added.
translations.idiomatic: If Sifu and Jue are guilty, demote them further.

sentences.zh: 必不可容，亦當先行訊鞫，俟罪狀著白，誅之未晩。

translations.literal: If they absolutely cannot be tolerated, there should still first be interrogation; wait until guilt is clear and execute—not late.
translations.idiomatic: If they must die, interrogate them first and execute when guilt is proven.

sentences.zh: 今不謀於臣等，遽遣使誅之，人情莫不震駭。

translations.literal: Now, without consulting us, envoys were hastily sent to execute them; everyone's feelings are shaken with terror.
translations.idiomatic: To send executioners without consulting us terrifies everyone.

sentences.zh: 願開延英賜對。」

translations.literal: We wish an audience at Yanying."
translations.idiomatic: We beg an audience at Yanying Hall."

sentences.zh: 至晡時，開延英，召德裕等入。

translations.literal: By the time of the afternoon audience Yanying was opened and Deyu and the others were summoned in.
translations.idiomatic: That afternoon Yanying was opened and Deyu was summoned.

sentences.zh: 德裕等泣涕極言：「陛下宜重慎此舉，毋致後悔！」

translations.literal: Deyu and the others wept and said with utmost urgency: "Your Majesty should weigh this act heavily and not bring regret!"
translations.idiomatic: Deyu wept and begged, "Your Majesty must weigh this act carefully lest you regret it!"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕不悔！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I do not regret it!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I will not regret it!"

sentences.zh: 三命之坐，德裕等曰：「臣等願陛下免二人於死，勿使既死而眾以爲冤。

translations.literal: Three times he ordered them to sit; Deyu and the others said: "We wish Your Majesty to spare the two men death and not let the multitude afterward think it injustice once they are dead.
translations.idiomatic: Three times he ordered them to sit. Deyu said, "Spare their lives so the people will not call it murder after they are dead.

sentences.zh: 今未奉聖旨，臣等不敢坐。」

translations.literal: Now we have not received the sacred command; we dare not sit.
translations.idiomatic: We dare not sit without your command."

sentences.zh: 久之，上乃曰：「特爲卿等釋之。」

translations.literal: After a long while the emperor finally said: "Specially for you I release them."
translations.idiomatic: At last the emperor said, "For your sake alone I spare them."

sentences.zh: 德裕等躍下階舞蹈。

translations.literal: Deyu and the others leaped down the steps and danced.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu and the others leaped down and danced for joy.

sentences.zh: 上召升坐，歎曰：「朕嗣位之際，宰相何嘗比數！

translations.literal: The emperor summoned them to ascend and sit and sighed: "At my succession the chief ministers—when did they ever count!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed, "At my succession, did my ministers ever count for anything?

sentences.zh: 李玨、季陵志在陳王，嗣復、弘逸志在安王。

translations.literal: Li Jue and Jiling favored Prince of Chen; Sifu and Hongyi favored Prince of An.
translations.idiomatic: Jue and Jiling favored Prince of Chen; Sifu and Hongyi favored Prince of An.

sentences.zh: 陳王猶是文宗遺意，安王則專附楊妃。

translations.literal: Prince of Chen was still the late emperor's wish; Prince of An solely attached to Consort Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen still reflected Wenzong's wish; An relied wholly on Consort Yang.

sentences.zh: 嗣復仍與妃書云：『姑何不效則天臨朝！』

translations.literal: Sifu even wrote to the consort: 'Aunt, why not imitate Wu Zetian in holding court!'
translations.idiomatic: Sifu even wrote Yang, 'Why not rule from court like Wu Zetian?'

sentences.zh: 向使安王得志，朕那復有今日？」

translations.literal: Had Prince of An gained his aim, how could I have today?"
translations.idiomatic: Had An won, would I be emperor today?"

sentences.zh: 德裕等曰：「茲事暖昧，虛實難知。」

translations.literal: Deyu and the others said: "This affair is obscure; truth and falsehood are hard to know."
translations.idiomatic: Deyu said, "These charges are murky; who can know the truth?"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「楊妃嘗有疾，文宗聽其弟玄思入侍月餘，以此得通意旨。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Consort Yang once had an illness; Wenzong allowed her younger brother Xuanzi to attend her for more than a month; thereby he gained her intent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "When Yang was ill, Wenzong let her brother Xuanzi attend her for a month and won her favor.

sentences.zh: 朕細詢內人，情狀皎然，非虛也。」

translations.literal: I have questioned the palace women in detail; the circumstances are perfectly clear—it is no fabrication."
translations.idiomatic: I questioned the women of the inner palace closely, and the facts are plain; this is no slander."

sentences.zh: 遂追還二使，更貶嗣復爲潮州刺史，李玨爲昭州刺史，裴夷直爲驩州司戸。

translations.literal: Thereupon he recalled the two envoys and further demoted Sifu to prefect of Chaozhou, Li Jue to prefect of Zhaozhou, and Pei Yizhi to registrar of Huanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: With that he recalled the two executioners and demoted Sifu again to prefect of Chaozhou, Li Jue to prefect of Zhaozhou, and Pei Yizhi to registrar of Huanzhou.

sentences.zh: 夏，六月，乙巳，詔：「自今臣下論人罪惡，並應請付御史台案問，毋得乞留中，以杜讒邪。」

translations.literal: In summer, the sixth month, on yisi day, an edict stated: "From now on, when subjects speak of another's crimes and evils, all such matters should be referred to the Censorate for investigation; they must not petition to have papers held at court, so as to block slander and wickedness."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of summer, on yisi day, an edict declared: "Henceforth any subject who accuses another of wrongdoing must refer the case to the Censorate for inquiry; no one may ask to have the charge kept within the palace to shut out slander and faction."

sentences.zh: 以魏博留後何重順爲節度使。

translations.literal: He Zhongshun, acting military governor of Weibo, was made military governor.
translations.idiomatic: He Zhongshun, the Weibo regent, was appointed full military governor.

sentences.zh: 上命道士趙歸真於三殿建九天道塲，親授法菉。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the Daoist Zhao Guizhen to establish a Nine Heavens ritual arena in the Three Halls and personally confer talismanic registers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had the Daoist Zhao Guizhen build a Nine Heavens ritual altar in the Three Halls and personally confer ritual registers upon him.

sentences.zh: 右拾遺王哲上疏切諫，坐貶河南府士曹。

translations.literal: Wang Zhe, Right Reminder, submitted a memorial remonstrating sharply and was demoted to secretary of Henan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhe, Right Reminder of the Censorate, sent in a sharply worded remonstrance and was punished with demotion to a clerical post in Henan.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，加仇士良觀軍容使。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, Qiu Shiliang was made Commissioner of Army Supervision.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn Qiu Shiliang was promoted to commissioner of army supervision.

sentences.zh: 天德軍使田牟、監軍韋仲平欲擊回鶻以求功，奏稱：「回鶻叛將嗢沒斯等侵逼塞下，吐谷渾、沙陀、党項皆世與爲仇，請自出兵驅逐。」

translations.literal: Tian Mu, military commissioner of Tiande Army, and Wei Zhongping, army supervisor, wished to strike the Uighurs for merit and memorialized: "The Uighur renegade general Wamosi and others press upon the frontier. The Tuyuhun, Shatuo, and Tangut have been their hereditary foes; we ask to march out ourselves and drive them off."
translations.idiomatic: Tian Mu of Tiande Army and his army supervisor Wei Zhongping sought glory by attacking the Uighurs. They reported: "The Uighur renegades Wamosi and his followers are pressing the border defenses. The Tuyuhun, Shatuo, and Tangut have feuded with them for generations; we request permission to drive them off ourselves."

sentences.zh: 上命朝臣議之，議者皆以爲嗢沒斯等叛可汗而來，不可受，宜如牟等所請，擊之便。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the court ministers to debate it; debaters all held that Wamosi and the others had betrayed their khan in coming and should not be received; it would be best, as Tian and the others requested, to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor put the matter before the court. Most agreed that Wamosi and his men had turned on their khan and should not be sheltered; they favored Tian Mu's plan and said it would be best to attack at once.

sentences.zh: 上以問宰相，李德裕以爲：「窮鳥入懷，猶當活之。

translations.literal: The emperor asked the chief ministers; Li Deyu held: "A bird at the end of its flight that falls into one's bosom ought still to be spared.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor asked his chief ministers, Li Deyu said, "Even a bird so desperate it flies into one's arms deserves to live.

sentences.zh: 況回鶻屢建大功，今爲鄰國所破，部落離散，窮無所歸，遠依天子，無秋毫犯塞，奈何乘其困而擊之！

translations.literal: How much more so the Uighurs, who time and again rendered great service—now broken by a neighboring state, their tribes scattered, destitute with nowhere to turn, coming from afar to rely on the Son of Heaven, not violating the frontier in the slightest—why strike them in their distress!
translations.idiomatic: The Uighurs have served the throne repeatedly; now a neighbor has broken them, their clans are scattered, and they have nowhere left to go. They come from afar to seek the emperor's protection and have not touched our borders in the least—how can we strike them when they are at their weakest?

sentences.zh: 宜遣使者鎮撫，運糧食以賜之，此漢宣帝所以服呼韓邪也。」

translations.literal: We should send envoys to pacify them and transport grain to bestow upon them—this is how Emperor Xuan of Han won over Huhanye."
translations.idiomatic: Send envoys to reassure them and ship grain in relief—that is how Emperor Xuan of Han won over Huhanye of the Xiongnu."

sentences.zh: 陳夷行曰：「此所謂借寇兵資盜糧也，不如擊之。」

translations.literal: Chen Yixing said: "This is what is called lending arms to bandits and feeding robbers; it would be better to attack them."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yixing objected, "That is feeding the enemy and arming brigands. We would do better to attack."

sentences.zh: 德裕曰：「彼吐谷渾等各有部落，見利則銳敏爭進，不利則鳥驚魚散，各走巢穴，安肯守死爲國家用！

translations.literal: Deyu said: "Those Tuyuhun and the rest each have their own tribes; when they see profit they are keen and rush forward to vie for it, when profit fails they scatter like startled birds and fish, each fleeing to his nest—how would they die holding their ground for the state's use!
translations.idiomatic: Deyu replied, "The Tuyuhun and the others each have their own tribes. If profit beckons they race forward; if fortune turns they scatter like birds and fish to their lairs. None of them will stand and die for the empire's sake!

sentences.zh: 今天德城兵才千餘，若戰不利，城陷必矣。

translations.literal: Today Tiande city has barely more than a thousand troops; if battle goes ill, the city will surely fall.
translations.idiomatic: Tiande garrison has barely a thousand men. If battle goes badly, the fortress is lost.

sentences.zh: 不若以恩義撫而安之，必不爲患。

translations.literal: Better to comfort and settle them with grace and righteousness—they will surely not become a threat.
translations.idiomatic: Treat them with kindness and they will cause no trouble.

sentences.zh: 縱使侵暴邊境，亦須俟征諸道大兵討之，豈可獨使天德擊之乎！」

translations.literal: Even if they raid and ravage the borderlands, we must wait until armies from all circuits are mobilized to punish them—how can Tiande alone be sent to strike them!"
translations.idiomatic: Even if they do raid the frontier, we should wait until columns from every circuit can be assembled before we move. Tiande alone must not carry the fight!"

sentences.zh: 時詔以鴻臚卿張賈爲巡邊使，使察回鶻情偽，未還。

translations.literal: At the time an edict had appointed Zhang Jia, Grandee of Splendid Happiness, frontier inspector to investigate the Uighurs' true intentions; he had not yet returned.
translations.idiomatic: By then the court had already sent Zhang Jia of the Office of Diplomatic Reception as frontier inspector to weigh the Uighurs' intentions; he had not yet returned.

sentences.zh: 上問德裕曰：『嗢沒斯等請降，可保信乎？』

translations.literal: The emperor asked Deyu: "Can Wamosi and the others, in petitioning surrender, be trusted with certainty?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Deyu, "Can we trust Wamosi and his men when they offer to submit?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「朝中之人，臣不敢保，況敢保數千里外戎狄之心乎！

translations.literal: He replied: "Among men at court, this subject dares not guarantee anything—how much less dare I guarantee the hearts of barbarians thousands of li away!
translations.idiomatic: Deyu answered, "I would not guarantee even a court colleague's loyalty—how could I guarantee the hearts of nomads a thousand leagues away?

sentences.zh: 然謂之叛將，則恐不可。

translations.literal: Yet to call them renegade generals, I fear, will not do.
translations.idiomatic: Still, to label them renegades may be unjust.

sentences.zh: 若可汗在國，嗢沒斯等帥眾而來，則於體固不可受。

translations.literal: If the khan were still in his realm and Wamosi and the others led troops here, then by propriety they certainly could not be received.
translations.idiomatic: If their khan still ruled at home and Wamosi marched here at the head of an army, protocol would forbid receiving them.

sentences.zh: 今聞其國敗亂無主，將相逃散，或奔吐蕃，或奔葛邏祿，惟此一支遠依大國。

translations.literal: Now we hear their state is broken and chaotic with no lord; generals and ministers flee and scatter, some to Tibet, some to the Qarlugs—only this branch relies on the great state from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Now we hear their realm is in chaos without a master, their ministers fled—some to Tibet, some to the Qarlugs—and only this band has come far to lean on the throne.

sentences.zh: 觀其表辭，危迫懇切，豈可謂之叛將乎！

translations.literal: Reading their petition, its peril and urgency are earnest—how can they be called renegade generals!
translations.idiomatic: Their memorial reads desperate and sincere; to call them renegades would be wrong.

sentences.zh: 況嗢沒斯等自去年九月至天德，今年二月始立烏介，自無君臣之分。

translations.literal: Moreover, Wamosi and the others reached Tiande last year in the ninth month; Wujie was made khan only in the second month of this year—between them there was naturally no lord-and-subject tie.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Wamosi reached Tiande last September, while Wujie was not proclaimed khan until February—there was never any bond of ruler and subject between them.

sentences.zh: 願且詔河東、振武嚴兵保境以備之，俟其攻犯城鎮，然後以動力驅除。

translations.literal: I ask that Hedong and Zhenwu be ordered to keep troops ready and guard the borders against them; wait until they attack and violate towns and garrisons, then drive them off with mobilized strength.
translations.idiomatic: Order Hedong and Zhenwu to hold the frontier in strength and wait. Only when they actually attack a town should we muster full force to expel them.

sentences.zh: 或於吐谷渾等部中小有抄掠，聽自仇報，亦未可助以官軍。

translations.literal: If they commit small raids among the Tuyuhun and others, let those old enemies settle scores themselves—we must not aid them with imperial troops.
translations.idiomatic: If they only skirmish with the Tuyuhun and the like, let those hereditary enemies fight it out among themselves; we should not send imperial troops to help.

sentences.zh: 仍詔田牟、仲平毋得邀功生事，常令不失大信，懷柔得宜，彼雖戎狄，必知感恩。」

translations.literal: Also order Tian Mu and Zhongping not to seek merit and stir up trouble; always keep faith without breach, and treat them with proper gentleness—though they are barbarians, they will surely know gratitude."
translations.idiomatic: Tell Tian Mu and Zhongping not to seek glory or stir trouble. Keep faith with them and treat them fairly—even nomads will feel gratitude."

sentences.zh: 辛酉，詔田牟約勒將士及雜虜，毋得先犯回鶻。

translations.literal: On xinyou day an edict ordered Tian Mu to restrain officers, troops, and allied barbarians from attacking the Uighurs first.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou day the emperor ordered Tian Mu to keep his soldiers and allied tribes from striking the Uighurs first.

sentences.zh: 九月，戊辰朔，詔河東、振武嚴兵以備之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the first day of wuchen, an edict ordered Hedong and Zhenwu to keep troops ready against them.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the ninth month an edict told Hedong and Zhenwu to stand ready on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 牟，布之弟也。

translations.literal: Mu was Bu's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Mu was the younger brother of Tian Bu.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，盧龍軍亂，殺節度使史元忠，推牙將陳行泰主留務。

translations.literal: On guisi day the Lulong army mutinied, killed Military Governor Shi Yuanzhong, and raised barracks officer Chen Xingtai to manage affairs as regent.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi day the Lulong garrison revolted, killed Governor Shi Yuanzhong, and made barracks officer Chen Xingtai acting commander.

sentences.zh: 李德裕請遣命慰撫回鶻，且運糧三萬斛以賜之，上以爲疑。

translations.literal: Li Deyu asked to send envoys to comfort the Uighurs and moreover transport thirty thousand bushels of grain to grant them; the emperor was doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu urged sending envoys to reassure the Uighurs and shipping thirty thousand bushels of grain in aid; the emperor hesitated.

sentences.zh: 閏月，己亥，開延英，召宰相議之。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on jihai day, the Yanying Hall was opened and the chief ministers summoned to debate it.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai day in the intercalary month the emperor opened the Yanying Hall and called his chief ministers to counsel.

sentences.zh: 陳夷行於候對之所，屢言資盜糧不可。

translations.literal: At the place where they waited to respond, Chen Yixing repeatedly said that feeding robbers would not do.
translations.idiomatic: While waiting their turn to speak, Chen Yixing kept insisting that feeding the enemy was unacceptable.

sentences.zh: 德裕曰：「今徵兵未集，天德孤危。

translations.literal: Deyu said: "Now levies are not yet assembled; Tiande stands alone and perilous.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu said, "Reinforcements are not yet in place and Tiande stands alone and exposed.

sentences.zh: 倘不以此糧啖饑虜，且使安靜，萬一天德陷沒，咎將誰歸！」

translations.literal: If we do not use this grain to feed the starving barbarians and thereby keep them quiet, and if by any chance Tiande falls, to whom will the blame go!"
translations.idiomatic: If we withhold this grain from starving nomads and fail to keep them quiet, and Tiande should fall—who will bear the blame?"

sentences.zh: 夷行至上前，遂不敢言。

translations.literal: When Yixing reached the emperor's presence, he then dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: When Yixing came before the throne he said no more.

sentences.zh: 上乃許以谷二萬斛賑之。

translations.literal: The emperor then granted twenty thousand bushels of grain to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor authorized twenty thousand bushels of grain for relief.

sentences.zh: 以前山南東道節度使、同平章事牛僧孺爲太子太師。

translations.literal: The former military governor of Shannan East Circuit and co–chief minister Niu Sengru was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Sengru, former governor of Shannan East and chief minister, was made grand preceptor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 先是漢水溢，壞襄州民居。

translations.literal: Earlier the Han River had overflowed and destroyed the dwellings of people in Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier floods on the Han had wrecked homes across Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 故李德裕以爲僧孺罪而廢之。

translations.literal: Therefore Li Deyu held Sengru guilty and had him removed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu blamed him for the disaster and had him dismissed.

sentences.zh: 盧龍軍復亂，殺陳行泰，立牙將張絳。

translations.literal: The Lulong army mutinied again, killed Chen Xingtai, and raised barracks officer Zhang Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Lulong mutinied again, killed Chen Xingtai, and made barracks officer Zhang Zhong their leader.

sentences.zh: 初，陳行泰逐史元忠，遣監軍傔以軍中大將表來求節鉞。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Chen Xingtai drove out Shi Yuanzhong, he sent the army supervisor's aide with a petition from the army's great generals requesting the command baton.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Xingtai ousted Shi Yuanzhong he had the army supervisor's aide bring a petition from the senior officers asking for the command seal.

sentences.zh: 李德裕曰：「河朔事勢，臣所熟諳。

translations.literal: Li Deyu said: "The situation north of the Yellow River is something this subject knows well.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu said, "I know the ways of the Hebei frontier well.

sentences.zh: 比來朝廷遣使賜詔常太速，故軍情遂固。

translations.literal: Lately when the court sends envoys and bestows edicts it is always too quickly, and so army sentiment solidifies.
translations.idiomatic: Of late the court has confirmed rebel regimes too quickly, and that only hardens the garrisons' grip.

sentences.zh: 若置之數月不問，必自生變。

translations.literal: If they are left alone for several months without inquiry, changes will surely arise of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Leave them alone for a few months without a reply and quarrels will break out on their own.

sentences.zh: 今請留監軍傔，勿遣使以觀之。」

translations.literal: Now I ask to detain the army supervisor's aide and not send envoys, so as to observe what happens."
translations.idiomatic: Keep the supervisor's aide here and send no envoy—for now let us watch."

sentences.zh: 既而軍中果殺行泰，立張絳，復求節鉞，朝廷亦不問。

translations.literal: Soon after, the army did indeed kill Xingtai, set up Zhang Zhong, and again sought the command baton—and the court likewise made no response.
translations.idiomatic: As he predicted, the garrison killed Xingtai, raised Zhang Zhong, and again demanded the seal; the court still said nothing.

sentences.zh: 會雄武軍使張仲武起兵擊絳，且遣軍吏呉仲舒奉表詣京師，稱絳慘虐，請以本軍討之。

translations.literal: Just then Xiongwu Army commissioner Zhang Zhongwu raised troops to strike Zhong and moreover sent army clerk Wu Zhongshu to the capital with a memorial stating that Zhong was cruel and oppressive and asking to chastise him with his own army.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Xiongwu commander Zhang Zhongwu marched against Zhong and sent staff officer Wu Zhongshu to the capital with a memorial condemning Zhong's cruelty and asking leave to punish him with his own troops.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，仲舒至京師。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Zhongshu reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter Wu Zhongshu arrived at the capital.

sentences.zh: 詔宰相問狀，仲舒言：「行泰、絳皆遊客，故人心不附。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the chief ministers to question him on the facts; Zhongshu said: "Xingtai and Zhong were both itinerants, so men's hearts did not attach to them.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers were ordered to question him. Zhongshu said, "Xingtai and Zhong were outsiders, and the troops would not follow them.

sentences.zh: 仲武幽州舊將，性忠義，通書，習戎事，人心向之。

translations.literal: Zhongwu was an old general of Youzhou by nature loyal and righteous, versed in books, skilled in military affairs, and men's hearts turned to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwu is a seasoned Youzhou officer—loyal and upright, literate, and skilled in war—and the men look to him.

sentences.zh: 向者張絳初殺行泰，召仲武，欲以留務讓之，牙中一二百人不可。

translations.literal: When Zhang Zhong had just killed Xingtai, he summoned Zhongwu and wished to yield the regency to him, but a hundred or two in the barracks would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhong first killed Xingtai he called Zhongwu and tried to yield command to him, but a hundred or so barracks men refused.

sentences.zh: 仲武行至昌平，絳復卻之。

translations.literal: Zhongwu went as far as Changping; Zhong again turned him back.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwu reached Changping, but Zhong sent him back.

sentences.zh: 今計仲武才發雄武，軍中已逐絳矣。」

translations.literal: Now by my reckoning, Zhongwu has only just marched from Xiongwu and the army has already driven Zhong out."
translations.idiomatic: By now Zhongwu has barely left Xiongwu and the garrison has already expelled Zhong."

sentences.zh: 李德裕問：「雄武士卒幾何？」

translations.literal: Li Deyu asked: "How many soldiers does Xiongwu have?"
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu asked, "How many men does Xiongwu field?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「軍士八百，外有上團五百人。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Eight hundred soldiers, and besides them five hundred elite local troops."
translations.idiomatic: Wu answered, "Eight hundred soldiers, plus five hundred local militia.

sentences.zh: 德裕曰：「兵少，何以立功？」

translations.literal: Deyu said: "With so few troops, how can merit be achieved?"
translations.idiomatic: Deyu said, "So few men—how can they prevail?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「在得人心。

translations.literal: He replied: "It lies in winning men's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Wu replied, "Victory depends on winning hearts.

sentences.zh: 苟人心不從，兵三萬何益？」

translations.literal: If men's hearts do not follow, what good are thirty thousand troops?"
translations.idiomatic: If the men will not follow, even thirty thousand soldiers are useless."

sentences.zh: 德裕又問：「萬一不克，如何？」

translations.literal: Deyu asked again: "If by any chance they fail, what then?"
translations.idiomatic: Deyu pressed on, "And if they fail?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「幽州糧食皆在媯州及北邊七鎮，萬一未能入，則據居庸關，絶其糧道，幽州自困矣！」

translations.literal: He replied: "Youzhou's grain is all at Guizhou and the seven frontier garrisons of the north; if by chance they cannot enter the city, then hold Juyong Pass and cut off the grain routes—Youzhou will be trapped of itself!"
translations.idiomatic: Wu said, "Youzhou's stores lie at Guizhou and the seven northern garrisons. If they cannot take the city, hold Juyong Pass and cut the supply lines—Youzhou will starve itself into submission!

sentences.zh: 德裕奏：「行泰、絳皆使大將上表，脅朝廷，邀節鉞，故不可與。

translations.literal: Deyu memorialized: "Xingtai and Zhong both had great generals submit memorials, coercing the court and demanding the command baton—therefore they must not be granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu argued, "Xingtai and Zhong bullied the court through petitions and seized power by force; they must not be rewarded.

sentences.zh: 今仲武先自表請發兵爲朝廷討亂，與之則似有名。」

translations.literal: Now Zhongwu has himself first submitted asking to raise troops to put down rebellion for the court—to grant him the post would seem to have proper grounds."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwu, by contrast, asked permission to march for the throne; appointing him would look legitimate."

sentences.zh: 乃以仲武知盧龍留後。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhongwu was made acting regent of Lulong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwu was then made acting governor of Lulong.

sentences.zh: 仲武尋克幽州。

translations.literal: Before long Zhongwu captured Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwu soon took Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 上校獵咸陽。

translations.literal: The emperor conducted military hunts at Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hunted near Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 十一月，李德裕上言：「今回鶻破亡，太和公主未知所在。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Li Deyu submitted: "Now the Uighurs are broken and destroyed; Princess Taihe's whereabouts are unknown.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Li Deyu reported, "The Uighur realm is shattered and Princess Taihe is missing.

sentences.zh: 若不遣使訪問，則戎狄必謂國家降主虜庭，本非愛惜，既負公主，又傷虜情。

translations.literal: If we do not send envoys to inquire, the barbarians will surely think the state humbles its lord before the enemy camp and never truly cared—wronging the princess and wounding barbarian sentiment alike.
translations.idiomatic: If we send no envoy to inquire, the nomads will think the throne cares nothing for its own princess and has betrayed her—and that will poison every relationship on the steppe.

sentences.zh: 請遣通事舍人苗縝繼詔詣溫沒斯，令轉達公主，兼可卜溫沒斯逆順之情。」

translations.literal: I ask that Secretariat Interpreter Miao Zhen be sent with continuing edicts to Wamosi, to convey word to the princess and also to probe Wamosi's disposition toward loyalty or rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: Send interpreter Miao Zhen with an edict to Wamosi to reach the princess and learn whether Wamosi stands with us or against us."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 上頗好田獵及武戲，五坊小兒得出入禁中，賞賜甚厚。

translations.literal: The emperor was rather fond of hunting and martial games; boys of the Five Wards could enter and leave the forbidden quarters, and rewards were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor loved hunting and martial spectacles; youths of the Five Wards wandered freely through the palace and received lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 嘗謁郭太后，從容問爲天子之道，太后勸以納諫。

translations.literal: Once when paying respects to Empress Dowager Guo, he casually asked about the way of being Son of Heaven; the empress dowager urged him to accept remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Visiting Empress Dowager Guo, he asked her casually how an emperor ought to rule; she told him to heed counsel.

sentences.zh: 上退，悉取諫疏閱之，多諫遊獵。

translations.literal: After the emperor withdrew, he took out all remonstrance memorials and read them; many remonstrated against hunts and pleasure outings.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he read through the remonstrances on file—many warned against hunting.

sentences.zh: 自是上出畋稍希，五坊無復橫賜。

translations.literal: From then on the emperor went out hunting somewhat less often, and the Five Wards no longer received lavish gifts at will.
translations.idiomatic: After that he hunted less often, and the Five Wards lost their easy bounty.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，以中書侍郎、同平章事崔鄲同平章事，充西川節度使。

translations.literal: On guihai day Cui Tan, Vice Director of the Secretariat and co–chief minister, was made co–chief minister and military governor of Xichuan.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai day Cui Tan, vice director of the secretariat and chief minister, was confirmed as chief minister and sent out as governor of Xichuan.

sentences.zh: 初，黠戛斯既破回鶻，得太和公主，自謂李陵之後，與唐同姓，遣達干十人奉公主歸之於唐。

translations.literal: Earlier, after the Kirghiz had broken the Uighurs and taken Princess Taihe, claiming descent from Li Ling and sharing surname with Tang, they sent ten senior envoys to escort the princess back to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: After the Kirghiz crushed the Uighurs and captured Princess Taihe, they claimed kinship with Tang through Li Ling and sent ten senior envoys to return her to the court.

sentences.zh: 回鶻烏介可汗引兵邀擊達干，盡殺之，質公主，南度磧，屯天德軍境上。

translations.literal: Uighur Khagan Wujie led troops to intercept the envoys, killed them all, held the princess hostage, crossed the desert southward, and encamped on the borders of Tiande Army.
translations.idiomatic: Uighur Khagan Wujie ambushed the escort, killed every envoy, seized the princess, crossed the desert southward, and camped on Tiande's frontier.

sentences.zh: 公主遣使上表，言可汗已立，求冊命。

translations.literal: The princess sent envoys with a memorial stating that the khan had been established and requesting investiture.
translations.idiomatic: The princess sent word that Wujie had been proclaimed khan and asked the throne to confirm him.

sentences.zh: 烏介又使其相頡干伽斯等上表，借振武一城以居公主、可汗。

translations.literal: Wujie moreover had his chancellor Xieganjiasi and others submit a memorial asking to borrow a city of Zhenwu in which the princess and khan might dwell.
translations.idiomatic: Wujie also had his chancellor Xieganjiasi petition for a walled town at Zhenwu where he and the princess could settle.

sentences.zh: 十二月，庚辰，制遣右金吾大將軍王會等慰問回鶻，仍賑米二萬斛。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on gengchen day, an edict dispatched Right General of the Golden Crow Wang Hui and others to console the Uighurs and moreover granted twenty thousand bushels of relief rice.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen day in the twelfth month Wang Hui of the Golden Crow Guard was sent to console the Uighurs with twenty thousand bushels of rice.

sentences.zh: 又賜烏介可汗敕書，諭以「宜帥部眾漸復舊疆，漂寓塞垣，殊非良計。」

translations.literal: Khagan Wujie was also granted an imperial letter instructing him: "You should lead your tribesmen gradually to recover the old realm; drifting and lodging by the frontier walls is no good plan at all."
translations.idiomatic: The throne also wrote Khagan Wujie: "Lead your people back to your old lands. Lingering along the frontier is no lasting plan.

sentences.zh: 又云：「欲借振武一城，前代未有此比。

translations.literal: It also said: "To wish to borrow a city of Zhenwu—no previous age has had such a precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The letter added, "No precedent exists for ceding a fortress at Zhenwu.

sentences.zh: 或欲別遷善地，求大國聲援，亦須且於漠南駐止。

translations.literal: If you wish to relocate elsewhere to a good land and seek the great state's vocal support, you must still first halt south of the desert.
translations.idiomatic: If you seek another refuge under imperial protection, you must first halt south of the desert.

sentences.zh: 朕當許公主入覲，親問事宜。

translations.literal: I shall allow the princess to enter court for audience and personally inquire into affairs.
translations.idiomatic: I will receive the princess at court and hear the matter myself.

sentences.zh: 儻須應接，必無所吝。」

translations.literal: If aid is needed, nothing will be withheld."
translations.idiomatic: Whatever aid you need, I shall not refuse."

sentences.zh: 春，正月，以張仲武爲盧龍節度使。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Zhang Zhongwu was made military governor of Lulong.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring Zhang Zhongwu was appointed military governor of Lulong.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以回鶻屯天德、振武北境，以兵部郎中李拭爲巡邊使，察將帥能否。

translations.literal: Because the Uighurs were encamped on the northern borders of Tiande and Zhenwu, the court made Li Shi, director in the Ministry of War, frontier inspector to examine whether generals were capable.
translations.idiomatic: With Uighurs camped north of Tiande and Zhenwu, Li Shi of the Ministry of War was sent as frontier inspector to test the commanders' fitness.

sentences.zh: 拭，鄜之子也。

translations.literal: Shi was the son of Li Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi was the son of Li Fu.

sentences.zh: 二月，淮南節度使李紳入朝。

translations.literal: In the second month Li Shen, military governor of Huainan, entered court.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Huainan governor Li Shen came to court.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，以紳爲中書侍郎、同平章事、判度支。

translations.literal: On dingchou day Shen was made Vice Director of the Secretariat, co–chief minister, and overseer of revenues.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou day Li Shen was made vice director of the secretariat, chief minister, and head of the treasury.

sentences.zh: 河東節度使苻澈修把頭烽舊戍以備回鶻。

translations.literal: Fu Che, military governor of Hedong, repaired the old garrison at Batou Beacon to guard against the Uighurs.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong governor Fu Che restored the Batou Beacon garrison to guard against the Uighurs.

sentences.zh: 李德裕奏請增兵鎮守，及修東、中二受降城以壯天德形勢，從之。

translations.literal: Li Deyu memorialized asking to increase troops for garrison duty and to repair the eastern and central Accepting-Surrender Cities to strengthen Tiande's posture; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu asked for reinforcements and repairs to the eastern and central Accepting-Surrender cities to stiffen Tiande's defenses; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 右散騎常侍柳公權素與李德裕善，崔珙奏爲集賢學士、判院事。

translations.literal: Liu Gongquan, Right Regular Cavalier Attendant, had long been on good terms with Li Deyu; Cui Guan memorialized to make him academician of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies and chief of its affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gongquan, a right regular attendant, was an old ally of Li Deyu; Cui Guan had him named scholar of the Academy of Worthies and put in charge of its office.

sentences.zh: 德裕以恩非己出，因事左遷公權爲太子詹事。

translations.literal: Deyu, because the favor had not issued from himself, used the occasion to demote Gongquan to steward of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Because the appointment had not come through him, Deyu used a pretext to demote Liu Gongquan to steward of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 回鶻復奏求糧，及尋勘吐谷渾、党項所掠，又借振武城。

translations.literal: The Uighurs again memorialized seeking grain, and moreover demanding an accounting of what the Tuyuhun and Tangut had plundered—they again asked to borrow Zhenwu city.
translations.idiomatic: The Uighurs again asked for grain, demanded restitution for Tuyuhun and Tangut raids, and once more requested a town at Zhenwu.

sentences.zh: 詔遣內使楊觀賜可汗書，諭以城不可借，餘當應接處置。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched palace envoy Yang Guan to present the khan a letter, instructing him that the city could not be lent and that the rest would be handled as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent palace envoy Yang Guan with a letter telling the khan that no fortress would be ceded and that other requests would be handled as appropriate.

sentences.zh: 三月，戊申，李拭巡邊還，稱振武節度使劉沔有威略，可任大事。

translations.literal: In the third month, on day wushen, Li Shi returned from frontier inspection and said that Liu Mian, military governor of Zhenwu, had authority and strategy and could be entrusted with great affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on wushen day, frontier inspector Li Shi returned and praised Zhenwu governor Liu Mian as a man of authority fit for great tasks.

sentences.zh: 時河東節度使苻澈疾病，庚申，以沔代之。

translations.literal: At the time Fu Che, military governor of Hedong, was ill; on day gengshen Liu Mian replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong governor Fu Che was ill; on gengshen day Liu Mian replaced him.

sentences.zh: 以金吾上將軍李忠順爲振武節度使。

translations.literal: Li Zhongshun, Senior General of the Golden Crow, was made military governor of Zhenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhongshun, senior general of the Golden Crow Guard, was appointed governor of Zhenwu.

sentences.zh: 遣將作少監苗縝冊命烏介可汗，使徐行，駐於河東，俟可汗位定，然後進。

translations.literal: Director of Palace Construction Miao Zhen was sent to invest Khagan Wujie, ordered to travel slowly and halt at Hedong until the khan's position was settled, then advance.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Zhen of the palace works was sent to invest Khagan Wujie with orders to proceed slowly and wait at Hedong until the khan's status was settled.

sentences.zh: 既而可汗屢侵擾邊境，縝竟不行。

translations.literal: Before long the khan repeatedly raided the frontier; Zhen in the end did not go.
translations.idiomatic: The khan soon raided the border repeatedly, and Miao Zhen never went.

sentences.zh: 回鶻嗢沒斯以赤心桀黠難知，先告田牟雲，赤心謀犯塞。

translations.literal: Uighur Wamosi, because Chixin was fierce, cunning, and hard to know, first told Tian Mu that Chixin planned to violate the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Wamosi, finding Chixin treacherous and unpredictable, first told Tian Mu that Chixin meant to raid the border.

sentences.zh: 乃誘赤心並僕固殺之，那頡啜收赤心之眾七千帳東走。

translations.literal: Thereupon he lured Chixin together with Pugu and killed them; Neixiechuo gathered Chixin's seven thousand tents and fled east.
translations.idiomatic: He then lured Chixin and Pugu into a trap and killed them; Neixiechuo took Chixin's seven thousand tents and fled east.

sentences.zh: 河東奏：「回鶻兵至橫水，殺掠兵民，今退屯釋迦泊東。」

translations.literal: Hedong memorialized: "Uighur troops reached Hengshui, killing and plundering soldiers and civilians; they now withdraw and encamp east of Shijia Po."
translations.idiomatic: Hedong reported, "Uighur troops reached Hengshui, killing and looting, and now camp east of Shijia Po."

sentences.zh: 李德裕上言：「釋迦泊西距可汗帳三百里，未知此兵爲那頡所部，爲可汗遣來。

translations.literal: Li Deyu submitted: "West of Shijia Po is three hundred li from the khan's headquarters; it is not known whether these troops are Neixie's division or sent by the khan.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu wrote, "Shijia Po lies three hundred li west of the khan's camp—we do not know whether these men follow Neixie or the khan.

sentences.zh: 宜且指此兵雲不受可汗指揮，擅掠邊鄙。

translations.literal: For the time being we should point to these troops as not obeying the khan's command and raiding the border on their own.
translations.idiomatic: For now blame these troops for defying the khan and raiding on their own.

sentences.zh: 密詔劉沔、武仲先經略此兵，如可以討逐，事亦有名。

translations.literal: Secretly order Liu Mian and Wu Zhong to first manage these troops; if they can be pursued and driven off, the affair will also have proper grounds.
translations.idiomatic: Secretly tell Liu Mian and Zhang Zhongwu to deal with this band first; if they can be driven off, the action will be justified.

sentences.zh: 摧此一支，可汗必自知懼。」

translations.literal: Break this one branch and the khan will surely know fear of himself."
translations.idiomatic: Crush this branch and the khan will learn fear."

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，庚辰，天德都防禦使田牟奏：「回鶻侵擾不已，不俟朝旨，已出兵三千拒之。」

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day gengchen: Tian Mu, commissioner of Tiande Defense, memorialized: "The Uighurs harass without cease; without waiting for court orders I have already sent three thousand troops to resist them."
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on gengchen day in the fourth month, Tiande commissioner Tian Mu reported, "The Uighurs keep raiding; without waiting for orders I have sent three thousand men against them."

sentences.zh: 壬午，李德裕奏：「田牟殊不知兵，戎狄長於野戰，短於攻城。

translations.literal: On day renwu, Li Deyu memorialized: "Tian Mu truly does not know warfare; the barbarians are long in field battle and short in storming cities.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu day Deyu protested, "Tian Mu knows nothing of war. Nomads excel in open battle and fail at sieges.

sentences.zh: 牟但應堅守以待諸道兵集，今全軍出戰，萬一失利，城中空虛，何以自固！

translations.literal: Mu should only hold firm and wait for troops from all circuits to assemble; now he sends the whole army to battle—if by any chance he is defeated, the city will be empty; how can he secure himself!
translations.idiomatic: He should hold the fortress until reinforcements arrive. If he risks his whole force and loses, the city is empty—how will he survive?

sentences.zh: 望亟遣中使止之。

translations.literal: I hope envoys will quickly be sent to stop him.
translations.idiomatic: Send envoys at once to stop him.

sentences.zh: 如已交鋒，即詔雲、朔、天德以來羌、渾各出兵奮擊回鶻，凡所虜獲，並令自取。

translations.literal: If battle has already been joined, then order Yun, Shuo, Tiande, and the rest to have the Qiang and Hun each send troops to strike the Uighurs with all their strength; whatever captives and booty they take, let them keep for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: If fighting has begun, let Yun, Shuo, Tiande, and allied Qiang and Hun tribes attack the Uighurs and keep whatever they capture.

sentences.zh: 回鶻羈旅二年，糧食乏絶，人心易動。

translations.literal: The Uighurs have been wanderers for two years; grain is exhausted and men's hearts are easily moved.
translations.idiomatic: The Uighurs have wandered two years; they are starving and restless.

sentences.zh: 宜詔田牟招誘降者，給糧轉致太原，不可留於天德。

translations.literal: It is fitting to order Tian Mu to entice those who surrender, give grain, and send them on to Taiyuan—do not keep them at Tiande.
translations.idiomatic: Order Tian Mu to entice defectors, feed them, and send them to Taiyuan—not Tiande.

sentences.zh: 嗢沒斯誠偽雖未可知，然要早加官賞。

translations.literal: Whether Wamosi's sincerity or falsehood is not yet knowable, he should early receive office and reward.
translations.idiomatic: Wamosi's loyalty is uncertain, but reward him early anyway.

sentences.zh: 縱使不誠，亦足爲反間。

translations.literal: Even if he is not sincere, it suffices for a stratagem of alienation.
translations.idiomatic: Even if he lies, the reward will sow distrust.

sentences.zh: 且欲獎其忠義，爲討伐之名，令遠近諸蕃知但責可汗犯順，非欲盡滅回鶻。

translations.literal: Moreover we wish to encourage his loyalty and righteousness and give a name to the punitive campaign, so that distant tribes near and far know that only the khan's rebellion is blamed—not that the Uighur people are to be wholly destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Honor his loyalty publicly so all tribes know we punish the khan's rebellion, not the Uighur people as a whole.

sentences.zh: 石雄善戰無敵，請以爲天德都團練副使，佐田牟用兵。」

translations.literal: Shi Xiong is peerless in battle; I ask that he be made Vice Commissioner of Tiande Defense to assist Tian Mu in employing troops."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xiong is unrivaled in battle—make him Tian Mu's deputy."

sentences.zh: 上皆從其言。

translations.literal: The emperor assented to all his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved every point.

sentences.zh: 初，太和中，河西党項擾邊，文宗召石雄於白州，隸振武軍爲裨將，屢立戰功，以王智興故，未甚進擢。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Taihe era, Tangut of Hexi disturbed the frontier; Wenzong summoned Shi Xiong from Baizhou, attached him to Zhenwu Army as adjutant; he repeatedly achieved merit in battle, but because of Wang Zhixing he was not greatly promoted.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taihe era Tangut raiders in Hexi had brought Shi Xiong from Baizhou into Zhenwu as a junior officer; he fought well but, owing to Wang Zhixing's influence, was not promoted far.

sentences.zh: 至是，德裕舉用之。

translations.literal: Now Deyu recommended and employed him.
translations.idiomatic: Now Deyu brought him forward.

sentences.zh: 甲申，嗢沒斯帥其國特勒、宰相等二千二百餘人來降。

translations.literal: On day jiashen, Wamosi led his state's teles, chancellors, and others—more than twenty-two hundred persons—to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen day Wamosi led more than twenty-two hundred followers, including teles and chancellors, to surrender.

sentences.zh: 上信任李德裕，觀軍容使仇士良惡之。

translations.literal: The emperor trusted Li Deyu; Army Supervision Commissioner Qiu Shiliang hated him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor trusted Deyu; Qiu Shiliang hated him.

sentences.zh: 會上將受尊號，御丹鳳樓宣赦。

translations.literal: When the emperor was about to receive the exalted title and proclaim amnesty from the Crimson Phoenix Tower,
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor prepared to receive his exalted title and proclaim amnesty from the Crimson Phoenix Tower,

sentences.zh: 或告士良，宰相與度支議草制減禁軍衣糧及馬芻粟，士良揚言於眾曰：「如此，至日，軍士必於樓前喧嘩！」

translations.literal: someone told Shiliang that the chief ministers and the treasury were drafting the edict to reduce the forbidden armies' clothing rations and horse fodder grain; Shiliang proclaimed to the crowd: "If so, on that day the soldiers will surely clamor before the tower!"
translations.idiomatic: someone told Shiliang the ministers planned to cut forbidden-army rations and fodder in the amnesty text. Shiliang warned the troops, "If that is true, we will riot before the tower on the day of the ceremony!"

sentences.zh: 德裕聞之，乙酉，乞開延英自訴。

translations.literal: When Deyu heard of it, on day yiyou he begged to open Yanying and explain himself.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu heard and on yiyou day begged an audience at Yanying Hall.

sentences.zh: 上怒，遽遣中使宣諭兩軍：「赦書初無此事。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and hastily sent palace envoys to announce to both armies: "The amnesty text never contained such a matter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and sent envoys to both armies: "The amnesty never mentioned such cuts.

sentences.zh: 且赦書皆出朕意，非由宰相，爾安得此言！」

translations.literal: Moreover the amnesty all issued from my intent, not from the chief ministers—how can you speak thus!"
translations.idiomatic: The text came from me, not the ministers—how dare you say this!"

sentences.zh: 士良乃惶愧稱謝。

translations.literal: Shiliang then was fearful and ashamed and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang was terrified and apologized.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，群臣上尊號曰仁聖文武至神大孝皇帝。

translations.literal: On day dinghai the ministers offered the exalted title Benevolent, Sagely, Martial, Civil, Supremely Numinous, Greatly Filial Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai day the court offered the title Benevolent, Sagely, Martial, Civil, Supremely Numinous, Greatly Filial Emperor.

sentences.zh: 赦天下。

translations.literal: An amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
translations.idiomatic: The empire was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 五月，戊申，遣鴻臚卿張賈安撫嗢沒斯等，以嗢沒斯爲左金吾大將軍、懷化郡王；

translations.literal: On day wushen, Grandee of Splendid Happiness Zhang Jia was sent to comfort Wamosi and the others; Wamosi was made Left General of the Golden Crow and Prince of Huaihua;
translations.idiomatic: On wushen day Zhang Jia was sent to comfort Wamosi, who was made left general of the Golden Crow and Prince of Huaihua;

sentences.zh: 其次酋長官賞有舉。

translations.literal: secondary chieftains received offices and rewards according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: his lieutenants received offices and rewards by rank.

sentences.zh: 賜其部眾米五千斛，絹三千匹。

translations.literal: His tribesmen were granted five thousand bushels of rice and three thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: His people received five thousand bushels of rice and three thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 那頡啜帥其眾自振武、大同，東因室韋、黑沙，南趣雄武軍，窺幽州。

translations.literal: Neixiechuo led his followers from Zhenwu and Datong, going east by way of Shiwei and Heisha, turning south toward Xiongwu Army, spying on Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Neixiechuo led his people east from Zhenwu and Datong through Shiwei and Heisha toward Xiongwu, aiming at Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 盧龍節度使張仲武遣其弟仲至將兵三萬迎擊，大破之，斬首捕虜不可勝計，悉收降其七千帳，分配諸道。

translations.literal: Lulong Military Governor Zhang Zhongwu sent his younger brother Zhongzhi with thirty thousand troops to meet and strike them, routing them utterly; heads captured and prisoners taken were beyond counting; all seven thousand tents were received in surrender and distributed among the circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhongwu sent his brother Zhongzhi with thirty thousand men, crushed them, and took countless prisoners; all seven thousand tents surrendered and were distributed among the circuits.

sentences.zh: 那頡啜走，烏介可汗獲而殺之。

translations.literal: Neixiechuo fled; Khagan Wujie captured and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Neixiechuo fled; Khagan Wujie caught and killed him.

sentences.zh: 時烏介眾雖衰減，尚號十萬，駐牙於大同軍北閭門山。

translations.literal: At the time Wujie's multitude, though diminished, still numbered a hundred thousand; he set his headquarters at Lümen Mountain north of Datong Army.
translations.idiomatic: Wujie still commanded a hundred thousand men and camped at Lümen Mountain north of Datong.

sentences.zh: 楊觀自回鶻還，可汗表求糧食、牛羊，且請執送嗢沒斯等。

translations.literal: Yang Guan returned from the Uighurs; the khan memorialized requesting grain, cattle, and sheep, and also asking that Wamosi and the others be seized and sent.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guan returned from the Uighurs; the khan asked for grain and livestock and demanded Wamosi be handed over.

sentences.zh: 詔報以「糧食聽自以馬價於振武糴三千石。

translations.literal: The reply stated: "Grain may be purchased with horses at Zhenwu for three thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: “The court replied that he might buy three thousand bushels of grain at Zhenwu with horses.

sentences.zh: 牛，稼穡之資，中國禁人屠宰；

translations.literal: Cattle are resources for planting; China forbids slaughter by the people;
translations.idiomatic: Cattle are farming stock and the empire forbids casual slaughter;

sentences.zh: 羊，中國所鮮，出於北邊雜虜，國家未嘗科調。

translations.literal: sheep are rare in China and come from northern allied barbarians—the state has never levied them.
translations.idiomatic: sheep are scarce in China and come from northern allies—the court does not tax them.

sentences.zh: 嗢沒斯自本國初破，先投塞下，不隨可汗已及二年，慮彼猜嫌，窮迫歸命。

translations.literal: Wamosi, from the first breakup of his state, first threw himself on the frontier and has not followed the khan for as much as two years; fearing their suspicion, he came in desperate straits to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Wamosi fled to us when his realm first collapsed and has not followed you for two years; he came because he feared you.

sentences.zh: 前可汗正以猜虐無親，致內離外叛，今可汗失地遠客，尤宜深矯前非。

translations.literal: The former khan precisely because of cruel suspicion without kinship caused internal division and external defection; now the khan has lost his land and lodges far as guest—you should especially deeply correct the errors of before.
translations.idiomatic: Your predecessor's cruelty drove his own people away; you have lost your land—do not repeat his mistakes.

sentences.zh: 若復骨肉相殘，則可汗左右信臣誰敢自保！

translations.literal: If flesh and blood strike one another again, then who among the khan's trusted ministers near at hand will dare preserve himself!
translations.idiomatic: If you slaughter kin again, which minister will dare stay at your side?

sentences.zh: 朕務在兼愛，已受其降。

translations.literal: I devote myself to inclusive love and have already accepted their surrender.
translations.idiomatic: I practice inclusive mercy and have already accepted them.

sentences.zh: 於可汗不失恩慈，於朝廷免虧信義，豈不兩全事體，深葉良圖！」

translations.literal: Toward the khan I do not lose gracious kindness; toward the court I do not impair faith and righteousness—is this not fulfilling both sides of the affair and deeply fitting a fine plan!"
translations.idiomatic: This honors both mercy to you and faith to me—is that not the wise course?"

sentences.zh: 嗢沒斯入朝。

translations.literal: Wamosi entered court.
translations.idiomatic: Wamosi came to court.

sentences.zh: 六月，甲申，以嗢沒斯所部爲歸義軍，以嗢沒斯爲左金吾大將軍，充軍使。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day jiashen: Wamosi's division was made the Army of Returning Allegiance; Wamosi was made Left General of the Golden Crow and army commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen day in the sixth month Wamosi's followers became the Army of Returning Allegiance under his command as left general of the Golden Crow.

sentences.zh: 門下侍郎、同平章事陳夷行罷爲左僕射。

translations.literal: Chen Yixing, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor of the Same Rank, was removed to Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yixing was demoted from co–grand councilor to left vice director.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，以尚書右丞李讓夷爲中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: Li Rangyi, Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Works, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor of the Same Rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Li Rangyi was made vice director of the Secretariat and co–grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 嵐州人田滿川據州城作亂，劉沔討誅之。

translations.literal: Tian Manchuan of Lanzhou seized the prefectural city and rebelled; Liu Mian punished and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Manchuan of Lanzhou rebelled and seized the city; Liu Mian executed him.

sentences.zh: 嗢沒斯請置家太原，與諸弟竭力扞邊。

translations.literal: Wamosi asked to settle his family at Taiyuan and with his brothers strive with all their strength to guard the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Wamosi asked to station his family at Taiyuan while he and his brothers guarded the frontier.

sentences.zh: 詔劉沔存撫其家。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Liu Mian to comfort and settle his family.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mian was ordered to care for his family.

sentences.zh: 烏介可汗復遣其相上表，借兵助復國，又借天德城，詔不許。

translations.literal: Khagan Wujie again sent his chancellor with a memorial borrowing troops to restore the state, and again borrowing Tiande city; an edict refused.
translations.idiomatic: Wujie again petitioned for troops to restore his realm and for Tiande city; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 初，可汗往來天德、振武之間，剽掠羌、渾，又屯杷頭烽北。

translations.literal: Earlier the khan had come and gone between Tiande and Zhenwu, raiding Qiang and Hun, and also encamped north of Batou Beacon.
translations.idiomatic: The khan had shuttled between Tiande and Zhenwu, raiding Qiang and Hun, and camped north of Batou Beacon.

sentences.zh: 朝廷屢遣使諭之，使還漠南，可汗不奉詔。

translations.literal: The court repeatedly sent envoys instructing him to return south of the desert; the khan did not obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: The court repeatedly told him to withdraw south of the desert; he refused.

sentences.zh: 李德裕以爲「那頡啜屯於山北，烏介恐其與奚、契丹連謀邀遮，故不敢遠離塞下。

translations.literal: Li Deyu held that "Neixiechuo encamps north of the mountains; Wujie fears he will join with Xi and Khitan in plotting interception, and therefore dares not stray far from below the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu argued, "Neixiechuo camps in the northern hills; Wujie fears alliance with the Xi and Khitan and dares not leave the border.

sentences.zh: 望敕張仲武諭奚、契丹與回鶻共滅那頡啜，使得北還。」

translations.literal: I hope Zhang Zhongwu may be ordered to instruct Xi and Khitan to join with the Uighurs in destroying Neixiechuo, enabling him to return north."
translations.idiomatic: Urge Zhang Zhongwu to rally the Xi and Khitan to destroy Neixiechuo so Wujie can move north."

sentences.zh: 及那頡啜死，可汗猶不去。

translations.literal: When Neixiechuo died, the khan still did not leave.
translations.idiomatic: When Neixiechuo died, the khan still would not leave.

sentences.zh: 議者又以爲回鶻待馬價。

translations.literal: Debaters again held that the Uighurs were waiting for horse prices.
translations.idiomatic: Some said the Uighurs were waiting for payment for their horses.

sentences.zh: 詔盡以馬價給之，又不去。

translations.literal: An edict paid the full horse price, yet they still did not leave.
translations.idiomatic: The court paid the full horse price; they still stayed.

sentences.zh: 八月，可汗帥眾過杷頭烽南，突入大同川，驅掠河東雜虜牛馬數萬，轉斗至雲州城門。

translations.literal: Eighth month: the khan led his multitude past Batou Beacon to the south, burst into Datong River valley, drove off and plundered tens of thousands of cattle and horses of Hedong's allied barbarians, and fought their way to the gates of Yunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the khan crossed south of Batou Beacon, swept into the Datong valley, seized tens of thousands of cattle from Hedong tribes, and fought to the gates of Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 刺史張獻節閉城自守，吐谷渾、党項皆挈家入山避之。

translations.literal: Prefect Zhang Xianjie closed the city and held himself secure; Tuyuhun and Tangut all took their families into the mountains to avoid them.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Zhang Xianjie barred the gates; Tuyuhun and Tangut fled into the hills.

sentences.zh: 庚午，詔發陳、許、徐、汝、襄陽等兵屯太原及振武、天德，俟來春驅逐回鶻。

translations.literal: On day gengwu an edict ordered troops from Chen, Xu, Xu, Ru, Xiangyang, and other circuits to encamp at Taiyuan, Zhenwu, and Tiande, waiting until spring to drive off the Uighurs.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu day troops from Chen, Xu, Ru, Xiangyang, and other circuits were ordered to Taiyuan, Zhenwu, and Tiande to expel the Uighurs in spring.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，賜嗢沒斯與其弟阿歷支、習勿啜、烏羅思皆姓李氏，名思忠、思貞、思義、思禮；

translations.literal: On day dingchou, Wamosi and his younger brothers Alizhi, Xiwuchuo, and Luosi were all granted the surname Li and named Sizhong, Sizhen, Siyi, and Sili;
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou day Wamosi and his brothers Alizhi, Xiwuchuo, and Luosi received the surname Li and the names Sizhong, Sizhen, Siyi, and Sili;

sentences.zh: 國相愛邪勿姓愛，名弘順；

translations.literal: the state's chancellor Aiyewu was granted the surname Ai and named Hongshun;
translations.idiomatic: chancellor Aiyewu took the surname Ai and the name Hongshun;

sentences.zh: 仍以弘順爲歸義軍副使。

translations.literal: and Hongshun was moreover made deputy commissioner of the Army of Returning Allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Hongshun was made deputy commissioner of the Returning Allegiance Army.

sentences.zh: 上遣回鶻石戒直還其國，賜可汗書，諭以「自彼國爲紇吃斯所破，來投邊境，撫納無所不至。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Uighur Shi Jiezhi back to his state with a letter to the khan instructing: "Since your state was broken by the Kirghiz and you came to throw yourselves on the frontier, comfort and settlement have been lavished without limit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Shi Jiezhi back with a letter: "Since the Kirghiz broke your realm you have lived on our frontier, and we have sheltered you generously.

sentences.zh: 今可汗尚此近塞，未議還蕃，或侵掠雲、朔等州，或鈔擊羌、渾諸部。

translations.literal: Now the khan still lodges near the frontier and has not yet considered returning to your tribe, or raids Yun and Shuo and other prefectures, or strikes and plunders the Qiang, Hun, and other divisions.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you linger near the border, raid Yun and Shuo, and strike Qiang and Hun tribes.

sentences.zh: 遙揣深意，似恃姻好之情。

translations.literal: From afar I infer your deep intent seems to rely on marriage kinship.
translations.idiomatic: I suspect you rely on marriage ties with the throne.

sentences.zh: 毎觀蹤由，實懷馳突之計。

translations.literal: Whenever I observe your tracks, you truly harbor plans of sudden raid.
translations.idiomatic: Your movements show you still plan raids.

sentences.zh: 中外將相鹹請誅翦，朕情深屈己，未忍幸災。

translations.literal: Within and without, generals and ministers all ask to punish and cut you down; my feeling is deeply bent on restraining myself and I have not yet borne to rejoice in your disaster.
translations.idiomatic: My ministers urge attack; I have restrained them and refused to profit from your misery.

sentences.zh: 可汗宜速擇良圖，無貽後悔。」

translations.literal: The khan should quickly choose a fine plan and not bring later regret."
translations.idiomatic: Choose wisely before you regret it."

sentences.zh: 上又命李德裕代劉沔答回鶻相頡干迦斯書，以爲：「回鶻遠來依投，當效呼韓邪遣子入侍，身自入朝。

translations.literal: The emperor also ordered Li Deyu to reply on Liu Mian's behalf to Uighur Chancellor Xieganjiasi's letter, holding: "The Uighurs came from afar to rely on us; they should imitate Huhanye in sending a son to attend court and coming in person.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu also answered Chancellor Xieganjiasi for Liu Mian: "You came as suppliants; imitate Huhanye—send a prince to court and come yourself.

sentences.zh: 及令太和公主入謁太皇太后，求哀乞憐，則我之救恤，無所愧懷。

translations.literal: And when you order Princess Taihe to enter audience before the Grand Empress Dowager, begging pity in sorrow, then our relief and succor will be without shame in the breast.
translations.idiomatic: Let Princess Taihe plead before the grand empress dowager, and our aid will be generous.

sentences.zh: 而乃睥睨邊城，桀驁自若，邀求過望，如在本蕃，又深入邊境，侵暴不已，求援繼好，豈宜如是！

translations.literal: Yet you glare at the frontier cities, arrogant and self-willed as before, demanding beyond hope as if still in your own tribe, and again deeply enter the frontier, ravaging without cease, seeking aid while continuing friendship—how can it be thus!
translations.idiomatic: Instead you glare from the frontier, demand as if still at home, and keep raiding while begging friendship—how is that acceptable?

sentences.zh: 來書又雲胡人易動難安，若令忿怒，不可複製。

translations.literal: Your letter also says barbarians are easily moved and hard to settle; if you make them angry, they cannot again be controlled.
translations.idiomatic: You write that nomads are quick to rage and hard to pacify.

sentences.zh: 回鶻爲紇吃斯所破，舉國將相遣骸棄於草莽，累代可汗墳墓，隔在天涯，回鶻忿怒之心，不施於彼；

translations.literal: The Uighurs were broken by the Kirghiz; the whole state's generals and ministers leave bones scattered in the grass; tombs of qaghans through generations lie cut off at heaven's edge—yet Uighur wrath is not vented on them;
translations.idiomatic: The Kirghiz shattered you and left your dead in the grass; your qaghans' tombs lie far away—yet your wrath falls on us,

sentences.zh: 而蔑棄仁義，逞志中華，天地神祇豈容如此！

translations.literal: but you scorn benevolence and righteousness and give free rein to your will in China—how can heaven and earth and the spirits tolerate this!
translations.idiomatic: you scorn justice and ravage China—heaven and earth will not abide it!

sentences.zh: 昔郅支不事大漢，竟自夷滅，往事之戒，得不在懷！」

translations.literal: Of old Zhizhi did not serve the Great Han and was utterly destroyed in the end—the warning of past affairs—can it fail to be kept in the breast!"
translations.idiomatic: Remember Zhizhi, who defied Han and was destroyed—let that warning live in your heart!"

sentences.zh: 戊子，李德裕等上言：「若如前詔，河東等三道嚴兵守備，俟來春驅逐，乘回鶻人困馬贏之時，又官軍免盛寒之苦，則幽州兵宜令止屯本道以俟詔命。

translations.literal: On day wuzi, Li Deyu and the others submitted: "If according to the earlier edict the three circuits of Hedong and the rest strictly keep troops on guard and wait until spring to drive them off, taking advantage when Uighur men are weary and horses lean, and the imperial army is spared the bitter severe cold, then Youzhou troops should be ordered to halt encamped in their own circuit awaiting edict.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi day Deyu argued, "If we wait until spring as planned, when the Uighurs are weak and our men spared winter cold, Youzhou troops can hold in place until ordered.

sentences.zh: 若慮河冰既合，回鶻復有馳突，須早驅逐，則當及天時未寒，決策於數日之間。

translations.literal: If we fear that once river ice joins the Uighurs will again raid suddenly and must early be driven off, then we should decide within a few days while the weather is not yet cold.
translations.idiomatic: If we fear winter raids once the rivers freeze, we must decide within days, before the cold.

sentences.zh: 以河朔兵益河東兵，必令收功於兩月之內。

translations.literal: Adding Hebei troops to Hedong troops will surely achieve success within two months.
translations.idiomatic: Reinforce Hedong with Hebei troops and we can finish within two months.

sentences.zh: 今聞外議紛紜，互有異同，倘不一詢群情，終爲浮辭所撓。

translations.literal: Now we hear outside debate confused, each with differences; if we do not once consult all minds, we will in the end be swayed by empty talk.
translations.idiomatic: Outside opinion is divided; unless we consult widely, empty talk will paralyze us.

sentences.zh: 望令公卿集議。」

translations.literal: I hope the nobles and ministers may be assembled to debate."
translations.idiomatic: Summon the court to debate."

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 時議者多以爲宜俟來春。

translations.literal: At the time debaters mostly held that it was fitting to wait until spring.
translations.idiomatic: Most officials favored waiting until spring.

sentences.zh: 九月，以劉沔兼招換回鶻使，如須驅逐，其諸道行營兵權令指揮。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Liu Mian was made concurrent Commissioner for Summoning and Winning Over the Uighurs; if driving off was needed, troops of expeditionary columns from all circuits were temporarily placed under his command.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Liu Mian was named commissioner to win over the Uighurs, with command over all expeditionary columns if war came.

sentences.zh: 以張仲武爲東面招撫回鶻使，其當道行營兵及奚、契丹、室韋等並自指揮。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhongwu was made Eastern Commissioner for Pacifying the Uighurs; troops of his circuit and Xi, Khitan, Shiwei, and the rest were under his own command.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhongwu was named eastern pacification commissioner with command over his own troops and the Xi, Khitan, and Shiwei.

sentences.zh: 以李思忠爲河西党項都將回鶻西南面招討使，皆會軍於太原。

translations.literal: Li Sizhong was made Tangut General of Hexi and Southwestern Punitive Commissioner against the Uighurs; all were to assemble at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sizhong was named Hexi Tangut general and southwestern punitive commissioner; all were to assemble at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 令沔屯雁門關。

translations.literal: Liu Mian was ordered to encamp at Yanmen Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mian was ordered to camp at Yanmen Pass.

sentences.zh: 初，奚、契丹羈屬回鶻，各有監使，歳督其貢賦，且詗唐事。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xi and Khitan were subordinate to the Uighurs; each had supervising envoys who yearly collected their tribute and also spied on Tang affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi and Khitan had been subject to the Uighurs, who sent overseers each year to collect tribute and spy on Tang.

sentences.zh: 張仲武遣牙將石公緒統二部，盡殺回鶻監使等八百餘人。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhongwu sent barracks officer Shi Gongxu to command the two tribes and altogether killed more than eight hundred Uighur supervising envoys and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhongwu sent Shi Gongxu to lead both tribes and kill more than eight hundred Uighur overseers.

sentences.zh: 仲武破那頡啜，得室韋酋長妻子。

translations.literal: Zhongwu defeated Neixiechuo and obtained the wives and children of Shiwei chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: Defeating Neixiechuo, Zhongwu took Shiwei chiefs' wives and children hostage.

sentences.zh: 室韋以金帛羊馬贖之，仲武不受，曰：「但殺回鶻監使則歸之！」

translations.literal: The Shiwei used gold, silk, sheep, and horses to ransom them; Zhongwu would not accept and said: "Only kill the Uighur supervising envoys and they will be returned!"
translations.idiomatic: The Shiwei offered gold, silk, sheep, and horses as ransom; Zhongwu refused and said, "Kill the Uighur overseers and you may have them back!"

sentences.zh: 癸卯，李德裕等奏：「河東奏事官孫儔適至，雲回鶻移營近南四十里。

translations.literal: On day guimao, Li Deyu and the others memorialized: "The Hedong reporting official Sun Chou had just arrived and said the Uighurs moved camp nearly forty li farther south.
translations.idiomatic: “On guimao day Deyu reported that Hedong courier Sun Chou had arrived saying the Uighurs had moved camp forty li nearer the border.

sentences.zh: 劉沔以爲此必契丹不與之同，恐爲其掩襲故也。

translations.literal: Liu Mian holds that this must be because the Khitan will not act with them and they fear being taken in a surprise attack.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mian thought they feared the Khitan would not join them and moved to avoid ambush.

sentences.zh: 據此事勢，正堪驅除。

translations.literal: According to this situation, it is exactly fitting to drive them off.
translations.idiomatic: The moment favored expulsion.

sentences.zh: 臣等問孫儔，若與幽州合勢，迫逐回鶻，更須益幾兵。

translations.literal: This subject and the others asked Sun Chou: if we join forces with Youzhou to pursue the Uighurs, how many more troops would be needed.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu asked Sun Chou how many more troops would be needed if Youzhou joined the pursuit.

sentences.zh: 儔言不須多益兵，唯大同兵少，得易定千人助之足矣。」

translations.literal: Chou said no great increase in troops was needed; only Datong had few troops and a thousand men from Yiding to assist would suffice."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chou said few reinforcements were needed—only a thousand men from Yiding to help understrength Datong."

sentences.zh: 上皆從之。

translations.literal: The emperor assented to all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 詔河東、幽州、振武、天德各出大兵，移營稍前，以迫回鶻。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Hedong, Youzhou, Zhenwu, and Tiande each to send out great armies, move camps somewhat forward, and press the Uighurs.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong, Youzhou, Zhenwu, and Tiande were each ordered to advance camps and press the Uighurs.

sentences.zh: 上聞太子少傅白居易名，欲相之，以問李德裕。

translations.literal: The emperor heard the name of Bai Juyi, Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, and wished to make him chief minister; he asked Li Deyu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard of Bai Juyi and wanted him as chief minister; he asked Deyu.

sentences.zh: 德裕素惡居易，乃言居易衰病，不任朝謁。

translations.literal: Deyu had long hated Juyi and thereupon said Juyi was aged and ill and unfit for court audience.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu, who disliked Juyi, said he was old and ill and unfit for court.

sentences.zh: 其從父弟左司員外郎敏中，辭學不減居易，且有器識。

translations.literal: His cousin's son, Left Department Acting Director Minzhong, was no less in literary learning than Juyi and moreover had capacity and insight.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Minzhong, a left department official, matched Juyi's learning and had better judgment.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，以敏中爲翰林學士。

translations.literal: On day jiachen, Minzhong was made Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen day Minzhong was made Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 李思忠請與契苾、沙陀、吐谷渾六千騎合勢擊回鶻。

translations.literal: Li Sizhong asked to join with Qibi, Shatuo, and Tuyuhun in six thousand horsemen to combine strength and strike the Uighurs.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sizhong asked to lead six thousand Qibi, Shatuo, and Tuyuhun horsemen against the Uighurs.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，以銀州刺史何清朝、蔚州刺史契苾通分將河東蕃兵詣振武，受李思忠指揮。

translations.literal: On day yisi, Yinzhou Prefect He Qingchao and Yu Prefect Qibi Tong were ordered to command Hedong tribal troops to Zhenwu under Li Sizhong's command.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi day He Qingchao of Yinzhou and Qibi Tong of Yu were sent with Hedong tribal troops to Zhenwu under Li Sizhong.

sentences.zh: 通，何力之五世孫。

translations.literal: Tong was the fifth-generation descendant of Heli.
translations.idiomatic: Tong was a fifth-generation descendant of Heli.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丁卯，立皇子峴爲益王，岐爲兗王。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day dingmao: the emperor's sons Xian and Qi were established as Prince of Yi and Prince of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on dingmao day, Princes Xian and Qi were enfeoffed as Prince of Yi and Prince of Yan.

sentences.zh: 黠戛斯遣將軍踏布合祖等至天德軍，言「先遣都呂施合等奉公主歸之大唐，至今無聲問，不知得達，或爲奸人所隔。

translations.literal: The Kirghiz sent General Tabuhezu and others to Tiande Army, saying: "Earlier we dispatched Dulüshihe and others to escort the princess back to Great Tang; to this day there has been no word—whether she reached or was cut off by wicked men is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Kirghiz general Tabuhezu came to Tiande and said, "We sent Dulüshihe to return the princess to Tang, but have heard nothing—whether she arrived or was blocked we do not know.

sentences.zh: 今出兵求索，上天入地，期於必得。」

translations.literal: Now we raise troops to seek her—above heaven, below earth, we are resolved to obtain her."
translations.idiomatic: We now search heaven and earth until we find her."

sentences.zh: 又言「將徙就合羅川，居回鶻故國，兼已得安西、北庭達靼等五部落。」

translations.literal: They also said: "We shall move to Heluo River and dwell in the Uighurs' old realm, and have already obtained five tribes including Anxi, Beiting, and Tatar."
translations.idiomatic: They also said they would move to the Heluo River in the Uighurs' old lands and had already absorbed five tribes including Anxi, Beiting, and Tatar."

sentences.zh: 十一月，辛卯朔，昭義節度使劉從諫上言，請出兵五千討回鶻，詔不許。
