translations.literal: Eleventh month, first day of xinmao: Liu Congjian, military governor of Zhaoyi, submitted that he asked to send five thousand troops to punish the Uighurs; an edict did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the eleventh month Liu Congjian asked to send five thousand men against the Uighurs; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 上遣使賜太和公主冬衣，命李德裕爲書賜公主，略曰：「先朝割愛降婚，義寧家園，謂回鶻必能禦侮，安靜塞垣。

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys to grant Princess Taihe winter clothing and ordered Li Deyu to write a letter to the princess, in brief: "The former court cut off love and sent you down in marriage, meaning to settle the homeland, holding that the Uighurs would surely be able to repel insult and keep the frontier quiet.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent winter clothes to Princess Taihe and had Deyu write her: "The former court sent you in marriage to secure the frontier, believing the Uighurs would guard the border.

sentences.zh: 今回鶻所爲，甚不循理，毎馬首南向，姑得不畏高祖、太宗之威靈！

translations.literal: Now what the Uighurs do is very much against reason; whenever their horse heads turn south, how can the princess not fear the awesome spirits of Gaozu and Taizong!
translations.idiomatic: Now they act without reason. When their horses turn south, do you not fear the spirits of Gaozu and Taizong?

sentences.zh: 欲侵擾邊疆，豈不思太皇太后慈愛！

translations.literal: If they wish to harass the frontier, do they not think of the Grand Empress Dowager's loving kindness!
translations.idiomatic: If they raid the border, do they forget the grand empress dowager's mercy?

sentences.zh: 爲其國母，足得指揮。

translations.literal: As mother of their state, you are fully able to command them.
translations.idiomatic: As their state's mother by marriage, you can command them.

sentences.zh: 若回鶻不能稟命，則是棄絶姻好，今日已後，不得以姑爲詞！」

translations.literal: If the Uighurs cannot obey orders, then they have cast off marriage kinship; from today onward they may not use aunt as an argument!"
translations.idiomatic: If they will not obey, they have broken the marriage bond—from today they may not plead kinship to the throne!"

sentences.zh: 上幸涇陽校獵。

translations.literal: The emperor conducted military hunts at Jingyang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hunted at Jingyang.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，諫議大夫高少逸、鄭朗於閣中諫曰：「陛下比來遊獵稍頻，出城太遠，侵星夜歸，萬機曠廢。」

translations.literal: On day yimao, Remonstrating Censors Gao Shaoyi and Zheng Lang remonstrated in the pavilion: "Your Majesty of late has hunted somewhat frequently, gone too far outside the city, returned when the stars were already setting, and neglected the myriad affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao day censors Gao Shaoyi and Zheng Lang remonstrated: "Your Majesty hunts too often, ranges too far, returns after nightfall, and neglects government."

sentences.zh: 上改容謝之。

translations.literal: The emperor changed expression and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor looked ashamed and apologized.

sentences.zh: 少逸等出，上謂宰相曰：「本置諫官使之論事，朕欲時時聞之。

translations.literal: When Shaoyi and the others withdrew, the emperor said to the chief ministers: "Remonstrating censors were originally set up to discuss affairs; I wish to hear them from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: After they left the emperor told his ministers, "I set up remonstrators to hear criticism whenever I need it.

sentences.zh: 宰相皆賀。

translations.literal: The chief ministers all congratulated.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers congratulated him.

sentences.zh: 己未，以少逸爲給事中，朗爲左諫議大夫。

translations.literal: On day jiwei, Shaoyi was made Supervising Secretary and Lang Left Remonstrating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei day Gao Shaoyi was made supervising secretary and Zheng Lang left remonstrating censor.

sentences.zh: 劉沔、張仲武固稱盛寒未可進兵，請待歳首，李忠順獨請與李思忠俱進。

translations.literal: Liu Mian and Zhang Zhongwu firmly said severe cold made advance impossible and asked to wait until the year's beginning; only Li Zhongshun alone asked to advance together with Li Sizhong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mian and Zhang Zhongwu insisted the cold forbade campaigning until the new year; only Li Zhongshun volunteered to advance with Li Sizhong.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丙寅，李德裕奏請遣思忠進屯保大柵，從之。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day bingyin: Li Deyu memorialized asking to send Sizhong to advance and encamp at Baoda Stockade; it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin day in the twelfth month Deyu asked to send Li Sizhong to Baoda Stockade; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，吐蕃遣其臣論普熱來告達磨贊普之喪，命將作少監李璟爲弔祭使。

translations.literal: On day dingmao, Tibet sent its minister Lun Pure to announce the death of Qaghan Damo; Director of Palace Construction Li Jing was made condolence envoy.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao day Tibet sent Lun Pure to announce Damo's death; Li Jing was sent as condolence envoy.

sentences.zh: 劉沔奏移軍雲州。

translations.literal: Liu Mian memorialized moving troops to Yunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mian moved his army to Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 李忠順奏擊回鶻，破之。

translations.literal: Li Zhongshun memorialized striking the Uighurs and defeating them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhongshun reported defeating the Uighurs.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，立皇子嶧爲德王，嵯爲昌王。

translations.literal: On day bingxu, the emperor's sons Yi and Cuo were established as Prince of De and Prince of Chang.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu day Princes Yi and Cuo were enfeoffed as Prince of De and Prince of Chang.

sentences.zh: 初，吐蕃達磨贊普有佞幸之臣，以爲相。

translations.literal: Earlier, Tibetan Qaghan Damo had favorite ministers whom he made chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: Tibetan Qaghan Damo had kept favorite ministers as chancellors.

sentences.zh: 達磨卒，無子，佞相立其妃絲林氏兄尚延力之子乞離胡爲贊普，才三歳，佞相與妃共製國事，吐蕃老臣數十人皆不得預政事。

translations.literal: Damo died without a son; the favorite chancellor installed the son of Empress Silin's elder brother Shang Yanli—Qilihu—as qaghan, only three years old; the favorite chancellor and the empress together controlled state affairs; several tens of Tibet's old ministers could not participate in government.
translations.idiomatic: Damo died childless; the favorites installed Silin's nephew Qilihu, aged three, while they and the empress ruled; dozens of elder ministers were shut out.

sentences.zh: 首相結都那見乞離胡不拜，曰：「贊普宗族甚多，而立絲林氏子，國人誰服其令？

translations.literal: Chief Minister Jieduna saw Qilihu and did not bow, saying: "The qaghan's clan has many men, yet you set up Silin's son—who among the people will obey his orders?
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Jieduna refused to bow to Qilihu and cried, "The qaghan's clan is full of men, yet you set up Silin's child—who will obey?

sentences.zh: 鬼神誰饗其祀？

translations.literal: What spirits will enjoy his sacrifices?
translations.idiomatic: What spirits will accept his offerings?

sentences.zh: 國必亡矣！

translations.literal: The state will surely perish!
translations.idiomatic: The state is doomed!

sentences.zh: 比年災異之多，乃爲此也。

translations.literal: The many disasters and portents of recent years are because of this.
translations.idiomatic: Recent disasters come from this.

sentences.zh: 老夫無權，不得正其亂以報先贊普之德，有死而已！」

translations.literal: This old man has no power and cannot correct the chaos to repay the former qaghan's grace—there is only death!
translations.idiomatic: I have no power to set this right and can only die to repay the former qaghan!

sentences.zh: 拔刀剺面，慟哭而出。

translations.literal: He drew his sword, slashed his face, and went out weeping bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: He drew his sword, cut his face, and left weeping.

sentences.zh: 佞相殺之，滅其族，國人憤怒。

translations.literal: The favorite chancellor killed him and exterminated his clan; the people were furious.
translations.idiomatic: The favorites killed him and wiped out his clan; the people were furious.

sentences.zh: 又不遣使詣唐求冊立。

translations.literal: They also did not send envoys to Tang to request investiture.
translations.idiomatic: They also sent no envoy to Tang for investiture.

sentences.zh: 洛門川討擊使論恐熱，性悍忍，多詐謀，乃屬其徒告之曰：「賊捨國族立絲林氏，專害忠良以脅眾臣，且無大唐冊命，何名贊普！

translations.literal: Strike Commissioner of Luomenchuan Lun Kongre was by nature fierce and cruel and full of crafty schemes; he therefore instructed his followers, telling them: "The traitors abandon the imperial clan and set up the Silin clan, exclusively harming the loyal and good to coerce the multitude of ministers, and moreover have no Tang investiture—what name of qaghan is this!
translations.idiomatic: Strike commissioner Lun Kongre, fierce and cunning, told his followers, "Traitors set up Silin's line, murder the loyal, and lack Tang investiture—what qaghan is this?

sentences.zh: 吾當與汝屬舉義兵，入誅絲林妃及用事者以正國家。

translations.literal: I shall with you and your sort raise righteous troops, enter and execute the Silin consort and those in power to rectify the state.
translations.idiomatic: I will raise righteous troops with you, kill the Silin empress and her ministers, and restore the state.

sentences.zh: 天道助順，功無不成。」

translations.literal: Heaven's way assists the obedient; merit cannot fail to be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven favors the righteous; we cannot fail.

sentences.zh: 遂説三部落，得萬騎。

translations.literal: He thereupon persuaded three tribes and obtained ten thousand horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: He won three tribes and ten thousand horsemen.

sentences.zh: 是歳，與青海節度使同盟舉兵，自稱國相。

translations.literal: That year he joined Qinghai Military Governor in alliance and raised troops, styling himself state chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: That year he allied with the Qinghai governor, took the title state chancellor, and marched.

sentences.zh: 至渭州，遇國相尚思羅屯薄寒山，恐熱擊之，思羅棄輜重西奔松州。

translations.literal: Reaching Weizhou he encountered State Chancellor Shang Siluo encamped at Bohen Mountain; Kongre struck him and Siluo abandoned baggage and fled west to Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At Weizhou he met chancellor Shang Siluo at Bohen Mountain, routed him, and drove him west toward Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 恐熱遂屠渭州。

translations.literal: Kongre then slaughtered Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kongre then sacked Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 思羅發蘇毘、吐谷渾、羊同等兵，合八萬，保洮水，焚橋拒之。

translations.literal: Siluo mobilized Supi, Tuyuhun, Yangtong, and other troops—eighty thousand in all—held the Tao River, burned the bridge, and resisted.
translations.idiomatic: Siluo rallied eighty thousand Supi, Tuyuhun, and Yangtong troops, held the Tao River, burned the bridge, and resisted.

sentences.zh: 恐熱至，隔水語蘇毘等曰：「賊臣亂國，天遣我來誅之，汝曹奈何助逆！

translations.literal: When Kongre arrived he spoke across the water to Supi and the others: "Traitorous ministers throw the state into disorder; heaven sent me to execute them—why do you aid rebellion!
translations.idiomatic: Kongre shouted across the water, "Traitors ruin the state; heaven sent me to kill them—why aid rebels?

sentences.zh: 我今已爲宰相，國內兵我皆得制之，汝不從，將滅汝部落！」

translations.literal: I am already chancellor; within the state I can command all troops—if you do not follow, I will destroy your tribes!
translations.idiomatic: I am already chancellor and command every soldier—defy me and I destroy your tribes!

sentences.zh: 蘇毘等疑不戰，恐熱引驍騎涉水，蘇毘等皆降，思羅西走，追獲，殺之。

translations.literal: Supi and the others hesitated and did not fight; Kongre led crack horsemen across the water; Supi and the others all surrendered; Siluo fled west, was pursued and captured, and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Supi hesitated; Kongre forded the river with elite cavalry; they surrendered; Siluo was caught and killed.

sentences.zh: 恐熱盡並其眾，合十餘萬，自渭州松州，所過殘滅，屍相枕藉。」

translations.literal: Kongre absorbed all their followers altogether—more than a hundred thousand—from Weizhou to Songzhou; wherever he passed he ravaged and destroyed; corpses lay piled one upon another.”
translations.idiomatic: Kongre absorbed their forces—more than a hundred thousand—and ravaged from Weizhou to Songzhou, leaving corpses heaped along the road.”
